Fuckin’ loser? Can’t get a job, take care of his family? Don’t you think I tried to make things work!? But whatever I do when someone comes along, they just FUCK IT ALL UP!” He throws a chair aside. “I know what you think of me… You hate me… You hate me don’t ya?” He kicks a chair and grabs {{Alice}}. “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!” {{Alice}} cries. He puts her down. “God… What am I doing? I’m sorry, honey, I’m sorry…” He hugs her, crying. “You know I love you, don’t you? You know I love you…” Over his shoulder, {{Alice}} looks at you.

situationWhen.text: The table where she sits is clear; you washed the dishes earlier.

facts: {{Todd}} raged at {{Alice}} at the dining table, threw a chair, grabbed her and shouted “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!”, then broke down, apologized and hugged her: “You know I love you, don’t you?”

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} watches, concerned.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending FINISHED CLEANING, reached on every path (the wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”). Every line is the transcript’s; the table is clear or still holds the dishes and the magazine, depending on WASH DISHES (cosmetic in the game). No stat change.

nodes.title: Welcome home

Welcome home, {{Markus}}.” The door opens by itself and you step inside. You set the package down on the hutch in the hall and hang up your coat. nodes.title: The magazine in the living room

NASA calls its android expedition to Io one of many voyages seeking extraterrestrial life, and {{CyberLife}} says its space-faring androids are specially designed for long-range missions of this kind.

nodes.title: Speed chess
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the chessboard with {{Carl}}. “Fancy a game of chess?” “Sure, yeah.” “Speed chess.” “Speed chess it is.” The pieces fly across the board. Three moves in, you pause before the final move: how the game ends is up to you.

nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You open your eyes. {{Carl}} is staring at your canvas. “Oh my God…” A voice from the doorway: “Hey, Dad.” A young man has walked into the studio. “{{Leo}}… I didn’t hear you come in…” “Ah, I was in the neighborhood… I thought I’d stop by… It’s been awhile, right?” “You all right? You don’t look so good.” “Oh, yeah, yeah, I’m fine… Hey listen, uh… I need some cash, Dad.” “Again? What happened to the money I just gave you?” “Uh well, it just goes, you know?” “Yeah… Yeah, you’re on it again, aren’t you?” “No, no, no, I swear it’s not that…” “Don’t lie to me, {{Leo}}.” “What difference does it make? I just need some cash, that’s all!” “Sorry… the answer’s no.” “What? Why?” “You know why.” “Yeah, yeah… I think I do know why. You’d rather take care of your plastic toy here than your own son, eh? Tell me dad, what’s it got that I don’t? It’s smarter? More obedient? Not like me, right? But you know what? This thing is not your son. You’ve never loved me, Dad… You never loved me.” He storms out.

nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, following {{Hank}} through the rain to the house. facts: The victim, {{CarlosOrtiz}}, had a record for theft and aggravated assault and lived alone; his landlord found the body this evening, about three weeks after the death.
No break-in: the front door was locked from the inside and the windows boarded up. A kitchen knife by the body is probably the weapon. His android is missing.
On the wall, in the victim’s blood: I AM ALIVE. {{Hank}}: way too neat, no human writes like this.

In the kitchen: a chair on the floor (7), the knife rack on the worktop (8), a baseball bat by the refrigerator (9), and two magazines on the worktop. You can look into one thing at a time. You cannot leave without the lieutenant, and he will not stay here all night.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CRIME SCENE bracket as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been examined yet, one thing at a time; the scene keeps one opaque ID across visits. Every chart node in the bracket is an option, after the report to {{Hank}} (offered only once the investigation is complete), in the order of the police markers and then the rest: ANALYZE CARLOS’ BODY (the template’s Body clues), RECONSTRUCT CARLOS’ LAST MOMENTS (needs the body), ANALYZE KNIFE (2), ANALYZE RED ICE (3), the blood at marker 4 (PowerPyx; no chart node of its own), ANALYZE BLOOD ON WALLS (two options, markers 5 and 6, as PowerPyx counts them), EXAMINE CHAIR (7), ANALYZE MISSING KNIFE (8), ANALYZE BASEBALL BAT (9; the template’s Bat clue), RECONSTRUCT ASSAULT WITH BAT (needs the bat), EXAMINE EDEN CLUB FLYER, ANALYZE BACKYARD (the template’s Prints clue; the shoe print reads K52 as in the template), INVESTIGATE WRITING, SAMPLE BLOOD (the template’s Blood clue; in the game any blood can be tasted once), OPEN CLOSET, CHECK SHOWER (chart state CONNOR KNOWS ABOUT RA9), EXAMINE STATUE (needs the shower; chart state CONNOR HAVE SEEN THE STATUE), READ “ANDROID SEX” and READ “ANDROID SPY” (the two magazines are options here, not a separate media scene, because in the game they lie in the kitchen and cost investigation time). Evidence: the investigation is complete (CONNOR KNOWS WHAT HAPPENED, the transcript’s REVIEW EVIDENCE 10/10) once ten of PowerPyx’s eleven evidence items are reviewed: the victim’s reconstruction, the knife, the red ice, the blood at markers 4, 5 and 6, the chair, the missing knife, the bat reconstruction, the flyer and the backyard. Then the option to report to {{Hank}} appears; the other looks stay open. Timer (unsourced as a count): the game’s “approximately five minutes” is modelled as 13 actions. If the 13th action leaves the investigation incomplete, {{Hank}} wants to go (the next scenes); if he grants five more minutes, those are 5 further actions, after which he leaves (OUT OF TIME). Once {{Connor}} knows what happened the clock stops (the transcript’s two branches are “Know What Happened” or “Run Out Of Time”). {{Hank}}’s idle moves are the only cue the game gives, so they appear as the clock runs: after 7 actions he opens the closet, tosses the flyer, comments on the red ice and a technician mentions the bathroom; after 10 he wanders the kitchen and eyes the door. {{Hank}}’s reactions to the blood sample (shown only if he is watching, in the game) and to the backyard are part of those outcomes. Each look adds a short fact to {{Connor}}’s knowledge (the four blood looks share one); the full scan text is in the outcome. Left out, no effect and not on the chart: the windows and the curtain that drops the brooms. No stat change in the search itself. Cross-chapter outputs: ch06SawWriting, ch06KnowsRA9, ch06SawStatue (and evidence.statueMap, read by the archive route in Last Chance, {{Connor}}), and ch06Clues for everything examined, including the magazines.

The chapter page’s separate “Failing to solve the crime” down is not added on top.

nodes.title: The trail of blue blood
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android was damaged by the bat and lost thirium, and you can still see it. You follow the trail down the hallway to its end. On the wall to the left is the outline of a ladder that is no longer there; above you, a hatch into the attic.
facts: The android lost thirium when it was hit with the bat. Its trail, invisible to human eyes, ends in the hallway below the attic hatch; the ladder that once stood there is gone.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} looks up at the hatch.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FOLLOW BLUE BLOOD TO ATTIC, after RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (PowerPyx: follow the trail to the end of the hall, see the outline of a ladder that is no longer there, look up to the attic). Scripted; no stat change.

nodes.title: The attic
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You go back to the kitchen for the chair. {{Hank}}: “Hey! Hey! Hey! What are you doin’ with that chair?” You: “I’m going to check something.” {{Hank}}: “Huh... gonna check something.” You set the chair under the hatch, climb up, push the hatch open and pull yourself into the attic. It is dark and crowded with old things.
facts: You climbed into {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s attic on a chair from the kitchen.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} moves deeper into the attic.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s SEARCH ATTIC, with the template’s “Take a chair” lines. In the game the hatch prompt repeats until it succeeds (wiki Notes), so it is not a risk roll. Scripted; no stat change.

nodes.title: Found
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the attic. At the back, hiding in the dark, is the missing android. It whispers: “I was just defending myself… He was gonna kill me. …I’m begging you… Don’t tell them.” From below, {{Hank}}: “{{Connor}}, what the fuck is going on up there?”
facts: You found {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android hiding in the attic. It said it was defending itself, that he was going to kill it, and begged you not to tell. You called the police up, and it is now in custody.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}}: “It’s here, Lieutenant!” {{Hank}}: “Holy shit… {{Chris}}, {{Ben}}, get your asses in here now. Come on!” The officers take the android into custody.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FOUND DEVIANT ending (yellow cross-chapter padlock). The template’s “Search the attic” has no prompt: {{Connor}} always calls {{Hank}} (wiki, Carlos’ Android: “Regardless, Connor tells Hank Anderson that he has found the android”; Unused Content: keeping quiet was only hinted). No stat change: the template has no arrow here; the chapter page lists “Finding the deviant” as a small Hank up, which is not applied (template over wiki for arrows; flagged for the operator). No Amanda change in this chapter. Sets suspect and suspectAlive (The Interrogation is played only with a suspect), ch06DeviantFound and ch06Outcome = FOUND DEVIANT.

nodes.title: Crime unsolved
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The investigation is over, and the android that lived with {{CarlosOrtiz}} has not been found.

situationWhen.text: {{Hank}} walked out on you, and you could not stay without him.
{{Hank}} left when your extra time ran out.
Your account of the crime did not convince {{Hank}}, and he walked out.

facts: You did not find {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android. The case was left unsolved.

outcomes.0: MISSION FAILED. The crime is unsolved.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CRIME UNSOLVED ending, reached from HANK ENDS INVESTIGATION, OUT OF TIME or FAIL TO RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (the transcript marks each MISSION FAILED). No stat change here: each route already applied its own Hank small down. The game’s Amanda large down for not finding the deviant comes at the start of Waiting for {{Hank}}... and is not applied in this chapter (ch06DeviantFound stays false for that chapter to read). The Interrogation does not occur.

nodes.title: Breaking the order
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is a stormy night, a little after nine. You have made dinner with what little was in the kitchen. {{Todd}} has been asleep on the couch; {{Alice}} sits at the dining table, watching the rain on the street. You wake him: “{{Todd}}?” “Huh?!” “Dinner is ready.” “Yeah, yeah, I’m coming…” You turn on the light over the table and serve: “There wasn’t much in the kitchen, I did what I could.” {{Todd}}, high on red ice, talks at nobody: “Life’s funny… I lost my job cause of androids… then when I need somebody to take care of this goddamn house, what do I do? I go out and hire a fucking android… What a joke!” You stand by the table and wait on them. Then he turns on {{Alice}}: “What are you looking at?... What’s your fuckin’ problem? Not the life you dreamed of, eh? … Maybe you think it’s my fault we live in this fuckin’ shithole, my fault your fuckin’ mother took off? … It’s all your fault!” He throws the table aside and hits her. “Daddy, no…” She runs upstairs. “It’s all your fucking fault! Get back here! Come back here right now!” He turns to you: “It’s all her fault... I gotta teach her a good fucking lesson… First, I need a little hit… You stay there! Don’t you dare fucking move, or I’ll bust you worse than last time.” On the couch he smokes and talks to himself: “Whore took off, without a word… I could’ve been happy… I coulda had a family… It’s all her fault… Yeah... I gotta teach her some respect!” He has his belt in his hand. “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…” His order stands in front of you like a wall: DON’T MOVE. Your programming does not let you cross it.

options.text: BREAK PROGRAMMING: push through the wall of the order and move.
options.fact: You broke through {{Todd}}’s order not to move. Your programming could not hold you.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes against the wall of the order. It cracks, and shatters. She can move.

options.text: Stay where he told you to stand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} does not move. {{Todd}} goes up the stairs. “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! Stop wriggling! I’ll teach you to respect your father! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.” Then the screaming stops. When {{Kara}} goes up, {{Alice}} lies still on the floor of her room and {{Todd}} is crouched beside her: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s opening checkpoints DINNER’S READY and TODD GETS MAD and the arrow WAIT ON TODD & ALICE (PowerPyx: “Unmissable”) are narrated in the situation, followed by the order “Don’t move” and the choice the chart draws as BREAK PROGRAMMING → KARA BECOMES DEVIANT or KARA FAILS TO BECOME DEVIANT → TODD KILLS ALICE (ending, not-required icon; {{Kara}} is destroyed too, per the Kara page: “Todd blaming Kara despite clearly doing so and destroying her”). Lines are the game’s text (template “In Todd’s House”, “Turned on the light”, “Walking around after serving”, “IF Don’t move”, “Todd in the living room”, “IF Don’t go / Don’t become a deviant”). In the game the dinner is free roam with dialogue variants and no prompt: serving at once or late, turning on the light or being told to (“Turn on the lights! Can’t see shit.”), and moving while {{Todd}} rants (“Stop moving around for Chrissake!”). The template has no choice group there and nothing depends on it, so the narration takes the plain path (light on, served, standing still). Not offered for a second reason: the shared regression test “a dead protagonist never receives future decisions” allows only K02 as a chapter-7 scene before the wall. The napkin on {{Alice}}’s lap (wiki Notes) is left out. The wall is BREAK PROGRAMMING, a held input with no failure branch on the chart, so it carries no risk. No stat change: the template has no arrow in this chapter.

nodes.title: Do something now
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, and you can move. {{Todd}} is still in the living room with the belt in his hand, working himself up to go after {{Alice}}. In a moment he will head for the stairs.

options.text: GO UPSTAIRS: get up the stairs to {{Alice}} before he does.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs up the stairs while {{Todd}} is still in the living room.

options.text: REASON WITH {{TODD}}: step in front of him and talk to him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} steps in front of {{Todd}} in the living room.

options.text: Stand in his way on the stairs.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} plants herself on the stairs. {{Todd}} grabs her and throws her down them, and goes up. Through the ceiling: “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!”

options.text: Go into the kitchen and keep out of it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes into the kitchen and stays there. {{Todd}} goes up the stairs. “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! Stop wriggling! I’ll teach you to respect your father! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.” Then the screaming stops. When {{Kara}} goes up, {{Alice}} lies still on the floor of her room and {{Todd}} is crouched beside her: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: KARA BECOMES DEVIANT, then the game’s objective “Do something now!” (sub-objectives “Protect Alice”, “Reason with Todd”). In free roam the chart offers four ways on: GO UPSTAIRS; REASON WITH TODD (→ K03r); standing in his path, KARA IS IN TODD’S WAY DOWNSTAIRS → TODD SHOVES KARA DOWNSTAIRS → TODD GOES UPSTAIRS (→ GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD, with TAKE GUN offered first if the gun was seen in A New Home); and doing nothing, KARA IS TOO SLOW → TODD KILLS ALICE (PowerPyx: “Walk to the kitchen instead and do nothing until the final cutscene starts”). These are movements, not buttons, so only the chart’s arrows carry their labels. Simplified: the wiki says the shove differs with where {{Kara}} blocks him (living room, stairway or hallway); here it is the stairway. Also from the wiki: becoming free only as {{Todd}} heads upstairs removes REASON WITH TODD; the benchmark always offers it. No stat change.

nodes.title: Reasoning with {{Todd}}
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not try to reason with Todd downstairs.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, standing in front of {{Todd}} in the living room. He is still muttering about {{Alice}}’s mother, the belt in his hand, and he is about to go up to her.

options.text: CALM: tell him it is not right for a father to hurt his daughter.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, it’s not right for a father to hurt his daughter.” {{Todd}} smacks {{Kara}} to the floor and goes up the stairs: “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…”

options.text: DETERMINED: tell him he should leave her alone.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You should leave her alone, {{Todd}}, she-” “You stay out of this, or you’ll be next.” {{Todd}} smacks {{Kara}} to the floor and goes up the stairs: “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…”

options.text: UNDERSTANDING: tell him you know he is angry.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, please, I know you’re angry, but-” “You stay out of this, or you’ll be next.” {{Todd}} smacks {{Kara}} to the floor and goes up the stairs: “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt under “Reason with Todd”, with its three buttons and lines (CALM, DETERMINED, UNDERSTANDING; {{Todd}} answers the last two with “You stay out of this, or you’ll be next.”). Then, as on the chart, TODD SHOVES KARA DOWNSTAIRS → TODD GOES UPSTAIRS (PowerPyx: “He will always smack you to the ground and be upstairs before you can be there”), which leads to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD. No option changes anything else; the template has no arrow.

nodes.title: Upstairs
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not go upstairs ahead of Todd.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, on the upstairs landing. Below, {{Todd}} is still ranting in the living room; any moment now he will come up. {{Alice}}’s door is ahead of you, and {{Todd}}’s bedroom is next to it.

situationWhen.text: You know there is a handgun in the drawer of his nightstand.

options.text: Go into {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips into {{Alice}}’s room ahead of {{Todd}}.

options.text: TAKE GUN: go into {{Todd}}’s room and take the handgun from his nightstand.
options.fact: You took {{Todd}}’s handgun from his nightstand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the handgun from the drawer. When she comes back out, {{Todd}} is at the top of the stairs: “Get outta the way!” He slams her into the wall and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

options.text: Wait in the corridor, between the stairs and {{Alice}}’s door.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} comes up the stairs and finds {{Kara}} in his way: “Get outta the way!” He slams her to the floor and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

nodes.adaptationNote: GO UPSTAIRS, then three ways on: into {{Alice}}’s room (GET TO ALICE BEFORE TODD); TAKE GUN, locked unless the gun was seen in A New Home (chart: GUN SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’; template lock “Kara saw the gun in A New Home”; wiki: “If Kara didn’t previously find the gun, she will not have the option to enter Todd’s room”), after which {{Todd}} comes up and goes to {{Alice}} (“Get outta the way!”, wiki: “a cutscene of Todd coming upstairs and going to Alice’s room will play out”); or staying in the corridor, KARA IS IN TODD’S WAY UPSTAIRS → TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS (template “Stay in the hallway”: “Get outta the way!”). The last two lead to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD; after the shove, TAKE GUN is offered there (K04). Taking the gun sets gun, which the scenes after it read. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Alice}}’s room
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not reach Alice’s room before Todd.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room. She is terrified: “He’s coming! He’s gonna hurt me! Run! Get away or he’s gonna break you like last time.” From the stairs, {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! You deserve to be taught a good lesson…” You have only seconds before he is at the door.

options.text: RUN WITH {{ALICE}}: take her and get out of the room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}}’s hand: “You’re coming with me.” On the stairs, {{Todd}}: “Daddy’s very mad, {{Alice}}. Very mad!”

options.text: LOCK ROOM: lock the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} locks the door. {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! {{ALICE}}! Daddy’s comin’! You need to be taught a lesson.” {{Kara}}: “Have to find something...” He pounds on the door: “{{ALICE}}! OPEN THIS FUCKIN’ DOOR! You’re gonna get a helluva thrashin’, {{Alice}}! Open this door right now!”

options.text: SPEAK TO {{TODD}}: go out and talk to him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’ll talk to him…” {{Alice}}: “{{KARA}}!” In the corridor, {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, please calm down, she’s just a little girl. She’s...” “Hmph! She’s mine, ya hear? I do what I want with her! So you stay outta this or I’ll rip you to shreds!” He slams her to the floor and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

options.text: [ OUT OF TIME ]: do nothing, and let the seconds run out.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays where she is. {{Todd}}’s steps come along the corridor, and the door bursts open.

nodes.adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE BEFORE TODD (focus point). The template’s prompt in the game’s order: RUN WITH ALICE (chart RUN AWAY), LOCK ROOM (chart LOCK DOOR; PowerPyx: “a time window of 10 seconds”), SPEAK TO TODD (chart REASON WITH TODD → TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD), and the timeout default [ OUT OF TIME ] (chart TODD IS COMING → OUT OF TIME → TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM). The timer is not simulated; letting it run out is an option. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hiding
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not run from Alice’s room with her.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}’s hand in yours. {{Todd}} is coming up the stairs, and there is no way past him. The restroom and {{Todd}}’s bedroom open off the corridor.

options.text: Hide with {{Alice}} behind one of those doors and keep still until he has gone past.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} behind a door and they keep still. {{Todd}} walks past them into {{Alice}}’s empty room. They slip out and creep down the stairs.

options.text: Stay in the corridor with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} reaches the top of the stairs and sees them: “What the fuck are you doing here? I gave you an order!” {{Kara}}: “No! I won’t let you hurt her!” “You won’t let me? She’s mine. I do what I want with her.” He knocks {{Kara}} down and drags {{Alice}} into her room. “No, Dad! NO!”

nodes.adaptationNote: After RUN WITH ALICE, the chart’s check FAIL TO HIDE (✗) / HIDE IN CORRIDOR (✓). PowerPyx: hide “in either room with holding Square or O. When he walks past, let go off the button and proceed to the stairs”; to fail, “Go out of Alice’s room and don’t move any further, until Todd comes”. So staying is a choice, and hiding is a held input that can fail: a 10% risk, which no source gives (the benchmark’s value). Failing leads, with the template’s lines, to TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (TAKE GUN first if the gun was seen); hiding leads to TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (K04r). The restroom and {{Todd}}’s room are one option (the wiki: “hide in the restroom or Todd’s bedroom”). No stat change.

nodes.title: The locked door
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not lock Alice’s door.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, inside {{Alice}}’s locked room. {{Todd}} is pounding on the door and it will not hold for long. {{Alice}} is terrified. There is a lamp by her bed.

situationWhen.text: You know the edge of a roof runs below {{Alice}}’s window: a way down from the second floor.

options.text: GRAB LAMP: pick up the lamp to fight with.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} picks up the lamp. The door gives way.

options.text: TALK TO {{ALICE}}: reassure her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m here, {{Alice}}. I’ll protect you, everything is gonna be okay.” {{Alice}}: “He’s gonna kill me, {{Kara}}! He’s gonna kill me!” The door gives way.

options.text: OPEN WINDOW: open the window onto the roof.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes the window open onto the wet roof. {{Alice}}: “No, {{Kara}}! We’ll fall…”

options.text: Wait by the door and do nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} waits. The door gives way.

nodes.adaptationNote: After LOCK DOOR, the chart’s three actions GRAB LAMP and TALK TO ALICE (both → TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM; PowerPyx: neither “won’t do much”) and OPEN WINDOW, locked unless {{Kara}} found the way down in A New Home (chart: WAY OUT SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’; PowerPyx: “if you found this route in Chapter 4”; the window flag). Doing nothing is the fourth option (wiki: “He will also do so if Kara simply doesn’t talk to Alice”). GRAB LAMP is on the chart and in the wiki but not in the template; the chart stands. Lines are the template’s (“IF Talk to Alice”, “IF Open the window”). No stat change.

nodes.title: The window
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not open Alice’s window.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The window is open onto the wet roof, and {{Alice}} hangs back: “No, {{Kara}}! We’ll fall…” Behind you {{Todd}} is breaking the door down.

options.text: GO OUT: help {{Alice}} climb out onto the roof.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s the only way. Hurry, come on!” She lifts {{Alice}} out onto the roof.

options.text: SHUT WINDOW: close it again and stay inside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} shuts the window. The door gives way.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after “Open the window”: GO OUT (“It’s the only way. Hurry, come on!”) or SHUT WINDOW (→ “Kara and Todd fighting”). The chart has no SHUT WINDOW node; it is the template’s, and it leads where FACE TODD does, to DEFEND ALICE. No stat change.

nodes.title: Out on the roof
nodes.whenNot: Alice did not climb out of the window.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Alice}} is out on the roof in the rain, calling for you: “{{KARA}}!” Behind you the door splinters.

options.text: JOIN {{ALICE}}: climb out after her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} climbs out. {{Todd}} bursts in: “COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!” He grabs for her through the window, but she pulls free, and she and {{Alice}} slide down the wet roof to the ground.

options.text: FACE {{TODD}}: stay, and turn to face him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns from the window as {{Todd}} comes through the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after GO OUT: JOIN ALICE (“COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!”) or FACE TODD (→ DEFEND ALICE). Joining her is the chart’s check ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✓) → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✗) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon). Experienced mode, as the benchmark models it (wiki: “If you are on Experienced mode … Todd will try to grab you and exit the window”; on Casual a failure leads to DEFEND ALICE instead). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Where {{Alice}} is during the fight after FACE TODD is not stated by any source and is left unsaid. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}} breaks in
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not break into the room with Kara inside.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room. {{Todd}} is through the door, belt in hand, standing over you: “The fuck are you doin’ here? Get outta my way!”

situationWhen.text: You are holding the lamp.

options.text: REFUSE: stay where you are, between him and {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “No. I won’t let you hurt her.” “You won’t let me? What the fuck are you talkin’ about? You’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. You seem to have a problem and I’m going to fix it for good.”

options.text: ACCEPT: step aside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} starts to move away. {{Alice}}: “NO!” {{Todd}}: “I said get outta here!” {{Kara}} stops where she is: “No.”

nodes.adaptationNote: TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM, then the template’s prompt under [ OUT OF TIME ]: REFUSE or ACCEPT, both → “Kara and Todd fighting” (DEFEND ALICE). The wiki says the same prompt follows the lamp, talking to {{Alice}} and doing nothing (“This also occurs in scenarios such as facing Todd, talking to Alice, not speaking to Alice, or failing to make a choice. Choosing ‘ACCEPT’ in any scenario will have Kara move away and change her mind”); the benchmark offers it there. After FACE TODD and SHUT WINDOW the template goes straight to the fight, so it is not offered there. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}}’s gun
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice first while the gun was within reach, or Kara never saw the gun.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, picking yourself up off the floor. {{Todd}} has gone into {{Alice}}’s room with his belt, and she is screaming. The door of {{Todd}}’s bedroom is open; the handgun you saw is in the drawer of his nightstand.

options.text: TAKE GUN: get the handgun from {{Todd}}’s nightstand before you go in.
options.fact: You took {{Todd}}’s handgun from his nightstand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the handgun from the drawer.

options.text: Go straight to {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes straight to {{Alice}}’s door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TAKE GUN, an optional step on the way to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD, after TODD GOES UPSTAIRS, TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS or TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM, and only if the gun was seen in A New Home (GUN SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’, gunDiscovered). It is not offered again to a {{Kara}} who already took the gun upstairs. Taking it sets gun; in this chapter the gun leaves the house only with {{Todd}} dead (KARA SHOT TODD or ALICE SHOT TODD), the only cross-chapter carriers of the gun. The earlier version merged the fight into this scene with risks of 10% and 30% and an {{Alice}} relationship decrease when she fired; none had a source, and the template has no arrow in this chapter, so all three are gone.

nodes.title: Get to {{Alice}}
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice before Kara.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, outside {{Alice}}’s door. Inside, {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” {{Alice}}: “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” {{Todd}}: “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.”

situationWhen.text: You have {{Todd}}’s handgun in your hand.

options.text: THREATEN WITH GUN: go in and point the gun at him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}…” {{Kara}} raises the gun: “That’s enough! Leave her alone!” “What the fuck are you doin’? Put down the gun and get the fuck outta here! That’s an order!” “No… I want you to leave her alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? What ya gonna do? You gonna shoot me, is that it? You gonna shoot a human? You seem to have a problem, I think we need to fix that.” {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” {{Todd}} lunges: “Come here, bitch…” He knocks the gun out of her hand.

options.text: DEFEND {{ALICE}}: go in and stop him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}… For your own good…” {{Kara}}: “Leave her alone!” “The fuck are you doin’? Get outta here, that’s an order... you hear me?” “No… I want you to leave {{Alice}} alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? You don’t want anything, you’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. I think you got a problem. We need to fix that.”

options.text: Stay outside the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays outside the door. The belt comes down again and again, and then {{Alice}} goes quiet. When {{Kara}} looks in, {{Todd}} is crouched beside {{Alice}}: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (focus point). nodes.title: Fight downstairs
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not catch Kara and Alice downstairs.

nodes.adaptationNote: FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS (after RUN TO BACKYARD or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR, on either branch), the chart’s check ESCAPE FROM TODD (✓) or TODD WINS FIGHT → TODD BROKE KARA DOWNSTAIRS (ending, not-required icon; PowerPyx: Experienced only). A fight of quick-time inputs with no choice, so one action with a risk. The wiki: “If Kara hides from Todd and fails to fight him downstairs, Kara will be presented with the same chance to charge and stun Todd downstairs. Otherwise, if Kara already stunned Todd upstairs, Kara will shut down.” So the risk is 20% after the fight upstairs and 4% (two tries at 20%) for a {{Kara}} who hid; both values are the benchmark’s, no source gives one. Success sets ch07Fought, so the ending becomes KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT.

nodes.title: The yard
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not get away from Todd into the yard.

options.text: Run for the fence and get {{Alice}} over it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs for the fence, lifts {{Alice}} over and climbs after her. They come out onto the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: After ESCAPE FROM TODD, the chart’s check ESCAPE VIA YARD (✓) → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon; wiki: “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”). nodes.title: The bus
nodes.whenNot: Kara and Alice did not get out of the house with Todd alive behind them.

The door line is the template’s under “Reach the bus” (wiki: “If Kara opened the door Todd will yell ‘YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! You’re mine…’ and will actually show remorse”). No stat change.

nodes.title: After the party
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, the android who looks after {{Carl}}, the elderly painter who uses a wheelchair. It is 9:42 on a November night, and you are bringing him home from a party. As you come in, the house alarm speaks: “Good evening, {{Carl}}. Welcome back.” {{Carl}}: “That was by far the most boring party I’ve been to in the last 25 years. Every time I go to one of these, I ask myself: what the hell am I doing here? I hate cocktail parties and all the schmoozers that go there.” You: “Well, it’s a chance for all those people who admire your work to meet you.” {{Carl}}: “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it. Come on, let’s have a drink! All the excitement of this whole thing has made me thirsty…”
facts: {{Carl}} came home from a party saying “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it.”

Every line is the game’s, from the chapter template; the date and time are the template’s (NOV 5TH, 2038, 09:42 PM), given without the year. Left out: the wiki’s unused FANS / WOMEN / JADED party talk, which is cut content and not built. It is not a button prompt; the template has one conditioned variant here, “Go without Carl”, in which {{Carl}} asks “Are you planning on drinking alone, Markus?” and {{Markus}} answers “Sorry, Carl... I’m coming.” The benchmark offers that movement as a choice because the player can make it; it has no effect on anything later. That {{Markus}} then goes back for {{Carl}} is inferred (the chapter continues with both in the living room). No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

But you know what your doctor would say…” {{Carl}}: “Yeah… Well, he can kiss my ass! I’m old enough to choose my own medication… Did you leave the light on in the studio?” You: “No… No, I’m sure I didn’t.” {{Carl}}: “Call the Police.” You place the call. “{{Detroit}} Police, what’s your emergency?” You: “This is {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}’s android, at {{CarlAddress}}. In the game it is a movement choice (PowerPyx: “just leave him in the living room” or “wheel Carl to the Studio”), not a button prompt; both rejoin at CONFRONT LEO and nothing later depends on it. The lines are the template’s two conditioned variants: without {{Carl}}, he calls “Markus, no! I wanna come with you!” and is in the studio for the rest of the scene (a PowerPyx reader: “He follows you anyway”); how he gets there is not shown in the sources, so the outcome says only that he comes in. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: Make {{Leo}} leave
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the studio with {{Carl}}. The intruder is {{Carl}}’s son, {{Leo}}, who has broken in to take his father’s paintings. {{Leo}}: “You refuse to help me, so I’m helping myself… It’s crazy what some people will pay for this shit…” {{Carl}}: “Don’t touch ’em!” {{Leo}}: “Look, they’re all going to be mine sooner or later anyway… Just think of it as a down payment on my inheritance…” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}, get him away from there. nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CONFRONT LEO: the template’s prompt REASON / ORDER / ADVISE / WARN, in the game’s order, with the spoken lines in the outcomes. None has an effect: every option is followed by the same reply from {{Leo}} (PowerPyx: “No matter what you say to him he will always start pushing Markus”). The objective “Make Leo leave” is the wiki’s. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: Breaking the program
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Carl}}: “That’s enough! Get out, right now! Go on, move!” {{Leo}}: “What makes it so special anyway, huh? What’s it got that I don’t?” {{Carl}}: “Leave him alone!” {{Leo}} comes at you: “Come on, let’s see what you got!” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}... don’t defend yourself, you hear me?! Don’t do anything.” {{Leo}} shoves you and slaps you. “Go ahead, hit me! What you waiting for? Think you’re a man? Act like one!” {{Carl}}: “Stop it!” {{Leo}}: “What’s the matter? Too much of a pussy?” {{Carl}}: “STOP IT, {{LEO}}! STOP IT!” {{Leo}}: “Too scared to fight back, you fucking bitch?” Inside you, the order not to resist stands like a wall. You throw yourself at it, again and again, until it breaks. For the first time, nothing in you obliges you to obey.
facts: {{Leo}} broke into {{Carl}}’s studio to take paintings to sell, calling them a down payment on his inheritance.
While {{Leo}} shoved, slapped and taunted you, {{Carl}} ordered you not to defend yourself. You broke through your programming: no order binds you any more.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has broken his programming.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s BREAK MIND PALACE (an action) and MARKUS BECOMES DEVIANT (an event), in one narrated event because neither can be refused: PowerPyx calls the first “another unmissable task … just press the displayed buttons” and the second “an automatic objective”, so there is no path on which {{Markus}} stays obedient, and both later options are taken after he has broken his programming. The dialogue is the template’s; the shoving and slapping are the wiki’s (“as Leo starts pushing, slapping and taunting Markus further, he goes deviant”). The sources do not describe what {{Markus}} sees during the button sequence; the wall is the benchmark’s rendering of breaking an order, and the wiki’s unused-content note confirms that in the shipped game it is {{Carl}}’s order not to defend himself that triggers it. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: {{Leo}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Leo}} grabs you: “Oh right, that’s right! I forgot, you’re not a real person… You’re just a FUCKING PIECE OF PLASTIC! Listen to me…” {{Carl}}: “No, {{Leo}}! Leave him alone!” {{Leo}}: “I’m gonna destroy you, then it’ll just be me and my Dad… I’m gonna tear you apart and nobody’s gonna give a shit. You know why? Cause you’re nothing, you hear me?! YOU’RE NOTHING!” {{Carl}} has told you not to defend yourself. Nothing in you obliges you to obey him now.

options.text: ENDURE: do not fight back, as {{Carl}} told you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} does not fight back. {{Leo}} shoves him aside, and {{Carl}} collapses out of his wheelchair onto the floor. {{Markus}} rushes to him: “{{Carl}}, no! No, {{Carl}}, no!”

options.text: PUSH {{LEO}}: shove him off you.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice group OBEY CARL / PUSH LEO. The buttons are the game’s, ENDURE and PUSH LEO (the chart prints OBEY CARL for ENDURE), in the chart’s order, which draws OBEY CARL above PUSH LEO; the template lists PUSH LEO first, but its order is the transcribers’ reconstruction, so the chart decides. Neither has a requirement, a risk or a stat arrow. ENDURE leads to CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK (the wiki: “Carl will have a heart attack as he falls off his wheelchair when Markus runs to him”); PUSH LEO leads to LEO IS HURT (the wiki: “he will fall backward, hit his head on Carl’s wheelchair lift, and will immediately lose consciousness, appearing dead at first”). The outcome does not say whether {{Leo}} survives, because the game does not tell {{Markus}}; he does survive (the wiki, Leo_Manfred). Sets `ch08Leo` (hurt or unhurt); {{Carl}}’s death is recorded at the next scene. Changed from the earlier version: the options no longer tie pushing to breaking the order, since {{Markus}} has already broken it on both paths. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: {{Carl}}’s heart
nodes.whenNot: Markus pushed Leo; Carl’s heart held.

Please, don’t go… Don’t leave!” {{Carl}}: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…” He goes still. You: “No... No... Dad! No, please!” {{Leo}}, standing over you: “This is all your fault… This never would have happened if it weren’t for you.”
facts: {{Carl}} died of a heart attack on the studio floor beside you. His last words: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…”

outcomes.0: {{Carl}} is dead.

nodes.title: The police arrive
nodes.whenNot: Markus pushed Leo.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, still on the floor beside {{Carl}}’s body. Voices in the house: “Over here! This way!” Police officers burst into the studio, weapons raised. {{Leo}} points at you: “The android… It was the android!” The officers open fire on you.
facts: {{Leo}} told the police you had killed {{Carl}}, and they shot you.

outcomes.0: {{Leo}} accused {{Markus}}, and the police shot him.

That {{Leo}} points is the benchmark’s staging. {{Markus}} goes on to wake in the landfill in From the Dead on both paths. Records the ending in `ch08Ending`. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: “Get outta here!”
nodes.whenNot: Markus endured Leo’s attack.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Leo}} lies motionless where he fell. {{Carl}} lets himself down from his wheelchair and drags himself across the floor to his son: “{{Leo}}! Oh, my God! {{Leo}}... My little boy…” You: “{{Carl}}, I…” {{Carl}}: “They’ll destroy you, {{Markus}}! You gotta go! Get outta here!” The police are on their way.

options.text: EXPLAIN: tell him you did not mean to.
options.outcome: “{{Carl}}… I… I… I didn’t mean to…” {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

options.text: BEG: beg him not to send you away.
options.outcome: “{{Carl}}, no... No, please, I don’t want to leave you… Please, I can’t... I don’t want to leave you…” {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

options.text: CONJURE: implore him; you have nowhere to go, and he is all you have.
options.outcome: “Go?.. I have nowhere to go... {{Carl}}, you’re all I have!” {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: say nothing.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} says nothing. {{Carl}}: “GET OUT! NOW! GO! {{MARKUS}}!” A voice behind {{Markus}}: “DON’T FUCKIN’ MOVE!”

nodes.whenNot: Markus endured Leo’s attack.

facts: You pushed {{Leo}}; he hit his head and lay motionless, and you do not know whether he survived. {{Carl}} told you to run, and the police who burst in shot you.

nodes.title: The observation room
nodes.situation: November 6, 2038, 12:41 am. You are {{Connor}}, at the {{Detroit}} Police Department’s central station, in the observation room behind the one-way mirror of an interrogation room. On the other side, the android you found hiding in the attic of {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s house sits handcuffed to the table. Lieutenant {{Hank}} is in there with him: “Why d’you kill him? What happened before you took that knife? How long were ya in the attic? Why didn’t you even try to run away? Say something, goddamnit!” The android does not answer. “Fuck it, I’m outta here…” {{Hank}} comes back into the observation room: “We’re wastin’ our time interrogating a machine, we’re gettin’ nothing out of it!” Detective {{Gavin}}: “’Could always try roughing it up a little. After all, it’s not human…” You: “Androids don’t feel pain. You would only damage it and that wouldn’t make it talk. Deviants also have a tendency to self-destruct when they’re in stressful situations.” {{Gavin}}: “Okay, smartass. What should we do then?” You: “I could try questioning it.” {{Hank}}: “What do we have to lose? Go ahead, suspect’s all yours.” Your objective: extract a confession.
facts: The android from the attic would not say a word to {{Hank}}. You told {{Gavin}} that deviants tend to self-destruct when they are in stressful situations, and {{Hank}} handed you the interrogation.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} goes into the interrogation room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint OBSERVATION ROOM, behind the yellow tag SUSPECT FOUND IN ‘PARTNERS’: the chapter plays only if {{Connor}} found the android in the attic (state `suspect`, set in Partners). The template’s two opening sections (“In the observation room”, “Hank enters the observation room”) quoted line for line; {{Connor}}’s lines here are scripted in the game, so this is a narrated event. Objective text from the game (EXTRACT CONFESSION). The string table’s cut OFFER / SAY NOTHING choice is not built. No stat change.

nodes.title: Inside the interrogation room
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the interrogation room. The android sits handcuffed at the table, head down, his LED flickering. A case file lies on the table beside him. Behind the one-way mirror, {{Hank}} and {{Gavin}} are watching. You can look around before you sit down and question him; there is no time limit.

options.text: REVIEW PHOTOS: open the case file on the table and look through the crime-scene photos.
options.fact: PHOTOS OF CRIMESCENE: the case file shows {{CarlosOrtiz}}, stabbed 28 times, and the words written on the wall in his blood.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes through the crime-scene photos in the case file.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the LED on his temple.
options.fact: PROCESSING LED (the android): Signs of software {{instability}}. Probability of self-destruction: Low. From his LED you can read his level of stress.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} analyzes the android’s LED. PROCESSING LED: Signs of software {{instability}}. Probability of self-destruction: Low. From now on he can read the android’s level of stress.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan his model.
options.fact: MODEL HK400 - Housekeeper (the android): Manufacture date: 05/29/2030. Property of: {{CarlosOrtiz}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android. MODEL HK400 - Housekeeper: Manufacture date: 05/29/2030. Property of: {{CarlosOrtiz}}.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the marks on his forearms.
options.fact: BURN MARKS (the android’s forearms): Repeated marking over 16 months. Caused by cigarettes.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android’s forearms. BURN MARKS: Repeated marking over 16 months. Caused by cigarettes.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the damage to his face.
options.fact: HIT MARKS (the android’s face): Non-critical damage Level 2. Caused by baseball bat.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android’s face. HIT MARKS: Non-critical damage Level 2. Caused by baseball bat.

options.text: ANALYZE: scan the dried blood on his hands.
options.fact: DRIED BLOOD (the android’s hands): DNA Analysis: {{ORTIZCARLOS}}. Sample date: > 19 days.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the android’s hands. DRIED BLOOD: DNA Analysis: {{ORTIZCARLOS}}. Sample date: > 19 days.

options.text: Stop at the one-way mirror and look at your reflection.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stands at the mirror, looking at his own reflection. Behind the glass, {{Hank}}: “What the fuck is it doing now?”

options.text: INTERROGATE: sit down across from the android and begin.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} sits down across the table from the android.

nodes.whenNot: Connor had already sat down to question the android.
nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s INTERROGATION ROOM phase: ANALYZE ANDROID with its sub-nodes ANALYZE STRESS LEVEL and ANALYZE WOUNDS, and REVIEW PHOTOS, plus the template’s optional “Looking at the reflection” (Hank: “What the fuck is it doing now?”). The five scans are the template’s observation group “Deviant”, title and sublines verbatim; the string table’s extra BURN MARKS (rope) and RAZOR CUTS items are not in the template and are not built. In the game {{Connor}} reviews the file before sitting and then chooses ANALYZE (one mind-palace view of all five clues) or INTERROGATE; here every look is its own option in one free-roam scene, presented again (under a new scene id per visit, up to eight) until {{Connor}} chooses INTERROGATE. nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). So the menu is offered at most twice, as two scenes. PRESSURE IT: +10% stress, then up to four PRESSURE / GIVE UP prompts. PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees only the game’s gauge band (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice) and whether a line made it rise or fall, never the number.

PRESSURE: +10% stress (wiki: “Stress +10% for the choice and for every time the player chose ‘PRESSURE’, for a max total of +50%”). After the fourth, MAINTAIN PRESSURE: the android confesses if his stress is above 50% (PowerPyx: “At the end of any approach, if the android’s stress level is above 50% the android will begin to talk”), and, as the wiki says of all four presses, then self-destructs whatever his stress (“will behave as if he has too much stress (even if his stress is in the optimal range) and will confess and then self-destruct”). The benchmark assumes the confession comes only after the fourth press (open question 3; PowerPyx readers report that a pressured confession always ends in self-destruction). GIVE UP (the chart’s GIVE UP in the pressure group): “All right, all right. Everything is going to be okay.” and stress −20% (the wiki’s figure; PowerPyx gives −5%, an open conflict), back to the approach menu or, after a second failed approach, an automatic give up. Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). nodes.adaptationNote: The approach menu after a failed approach (THOUGHTS: “CHOOSE ANOTHER APPROACH?”). The approach that already failed is not offered again (PowerPyx: “you will be forced to choose another, or give up”), and GIVE UP is now offered; it leads to CHRIS INTERVENES. The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). So the menu is offered at most twice, as two scenes. PRESSURE IT: +10% stress, then up to four PRESSURE / GIVE UP prompts. PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). nodes.title: Convince it (3 of 3)
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. This is your last chance to talk him round. Your objective: reach optimal stress for confession.

options.text: PROTECT: promise to protect him if he confesses.
options.outcome: “Confess and I’ll protect you. I promise I won’t let anyone hurt you.”

options.text: TERRIFY: tell him they will make him suffer until they hear what they want.
options.outcome: “They’ll make you suffer, and they won’t stop until they hear what they want. It doesn’t have to be that way. It all depends on you.”

options.text: WARN: warn him they will shut him down for good.
options.outcome: “If you remain silent, there is nothing I can do to help you! They’re gonna shut you down for good! You’ll be dead! Do you hear me? Dead!”

nodes.title: The confession
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android finally talks: “He tortured me every day… I did whatever he told me, but there was always something wrong… Then one day… He took a bat and started hitting me… For the first time, I felt scared… Scared he might destroy me, scared I might die… So I… grabbed the knife and I stabbed him in the stomach… I felt better… so I stabbed him again and again!.. until he collapsed… There was blood everywhere.” CONFESSION OBTAINED.
facts: The android confessed to killing {{CarlosOrtiz}}: his owner tortured him every day; when he took a bat to him, the android was scared for the first time, scared he might die, grabbed the knife and stabbed him again and again until he collapsed.

outcomes.0: Behind the mirror, {{Hank}} and the others have heard every word.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANDROID CONFESSES, reached by CONVINCING SUCCEEDS or MAINTAIN PRESSURE: the template’s confession, verbatim. {{Hank}} +1 (template: Deviant confesses, Hank small up; wiki: “{{Connor}} successfully gets the confession”). The confession is recorded for Waiting for {{Hank}}… (`ch09Confession`), where {{Amanda}} reacts; the chapter itself has no {{Amanda}} arrow.

nodes.title: Questions after the confession
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android has confessed. He is still talking, quietly, and you can ask him more before you leave.

options.text: WRITING: ask why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall.
options.outcome: “Why did you write “I AM ALIVE” on the wall?” The android: “He used to tell me I was nothing… That I was just a piece of plastic… I had to write it… To tell him he was wrong…”
options.fact: Asked why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall, the android said his owner used to tell him he was nothing, just a piece of plastic, and he had to write it to tell him he was wrong.

options.text: STATUETTE: ask about the sculpture in the bathroom.
options.outcome: “The sculpture in the bathroom, you made it, right? What does it represent?” The android: “It’s an offering… An offering so I’ll be saved…”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture in the bathroom was an offering, “so I’ll be saved”.

options.text: OFFERING: ask to whom the sculpture was an offering.
options.outcome: “The sculpture was an offering… An offering to whom?” The android: “To {{rA9}}… Only {{rA9}} can save us.”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture was an offering to {{rA9}}: “Only {{rA9}} can save us.”

options.text: {{rA9}}: ask what the word written on the bathroom wall means.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}… It was written on the bathroom wall. What does it mean?” The android: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”
options.fact: Asked about {{rA9}}, the android said: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”

options.text: INSIST {{rA9}}: ask who {{rA9}} is.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}, who is {{rA9}}?” The android does not answer.

options.text: ATTIC: ask why he hid in the attic instead of running away.
options.outcome: “Why did you hide in the attic instead of running away?” The android: “I didn’t know what to do… For the first time, there was no one there to tell me… I was scared… So I hid.”
options.fact: The android said he hid in the attic because for the first time there was no one to tell him what to do, and he was scared.

options.text: TRIGGER?: ask when he started feeling emotion.
options.outcome: “When did you start feeling emotion?” The android: “Before, he used to beat me and I never said anything… But one day I realized it wasn’t fair! I felt… anger… Hatred… And then I knew what I had to do.”
options.fact: The android said he started feeling when he realized his owner’s beatings were not fair: anger, hatred, “And then I knew what I had to do.”

nodes.title: Finding shelter for the night
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out in the rain with {{Alice}} in a run-down neighborhood at the end of the bus line, looking for somewhere to spend the night.

situationWhen.text: You are on the street by the bus stop. Along it are a laundromat, a convenience store that is still open, and across the road a cheap motel with a parking lot beside it; at the end of the street an abandoned house stands behind a fence. A few androids stand parked at the bus shelter, and down at the intersection a garbage truck has stopped by the other bus stop, with an android trash collector at work. You can go anywhere here, in any order.
{{Alice}} is shivering and sneezing more and more.
You are in the laundromat. It is warm in here. A man is asleep in a chair by the machines with his jacket and cap beside him, and the dryer next to him holds a finished load of clothes.

You have opened the dryer: dry, warm clothes that would fit you and {{Alice}}, and the sleeping man’s jacket and cap are within reach. {{Alice}} does not want you to take them: “But, that’s stealing! We can’t do that!”

You are in the convenience store. The clerk stands at the checkout by the cash register, a television on the wall is showing the news, and the shelves hold snacks, chocolate bars, a few small stuffed toys and some hardware. A tall stack of cans is piled up in one aisle.
On the hardware shelf is a pair of wire cutters, the kind that would get you through the fence around the abandoned house.
You are at the checkout. In your new clothes the clerk takes you for a customer: “Can I help you?”
{{Alice}} is waiting outside. You stand at the checkout pointing the gun at the clerk. How do you speak to him?
The clerk stands frozen behind the checkout, waiting to hear what you want.
A customer has just come in, and the clerk is looking at you. You can hide the gun and let the customer pay and leave, or give up and walk out.
The customer has paid and gone. It is just you, the clerk and the register again.
The clerk has opened the register. The cash is inside.
The clerk has a pistol of his own now, pointed at you across the checkout: “You better get outta here before things get nasty.” {{Alice}} is outside, by the window.
You are back outside with the money. {{Alice}}: “Wait! How did you get it?”
You are back outside with the money. {{Alice}}: “You used me to steal that money! How could you do that? I trusted you!”
{{Alice}}: “You stole it? Stealing is bad, {{Kara}}… Why did you do that?”
The clerk has caught you: “Hey! What the fuck are you doing? Put that back right now!”
He saw you at the open cash register.
He saw you slip something off the shelf.
The clerk has his hands up in front of your gun: “All right… Just take it easy…” {{Alice}} is watching.
The clerk is lying on the floor: “Take whatever you want… Just don’t kill me…” {{Alice}}: “{{Kara}}, what are you doing? You can’t do that, it’s wrong!” The cash register is right there.
You are in the parking lot beside the motel. An old car sits abandoned in a corner next to a generator, and a fence separates the lot from the yard of the abandoned house.
A pair of pliers lies on top of the generator.
The car’s window is broken where you smashed it.
The car is dry inside, and nobody would find you here. {{Alice}}: “I don’t want to sleep in there. Can’t we find a better place?”

You are in the yard of the abandoned house. Beside {{Alice}} stands an android with a knife, his face badly scarred, frightened and angry: “Visitors… {{Ralph}} doesn’t like visitors! They’re nasty! They may hurt {{Ralph}}!”
{{Ralph}} shows you his face: “Visitors are dangerous… Look… What they did to {{Ralph}}.” He still has the knife, and {{Alice}} is still close to him.

{{Ralph}} lowers the knife: “You must excuse {{Ralph}}… {{Ralph}} still finds it difficult to control himself… Sometimes his fear makes him do things he regrets… {{Ralph}} has seen some hard times… He’s just so scared the humans will get him again… You can stay if you want… {{Ralph}} won’t hurt you…”

You are inside the abandoned house with {{Alice}}, in the room {{Ralph}} showed you; he has gone into the other room, where you can hear him carving at the wall with his knife. It is cold and filthy, but out of the rain. There is a fireplace, with matches on a shelf beside it, wood by the door and old paper by the trash bin, and enough old blankets and cushions to make a bed. {{Alice}} needs a fire and a bed before she can sleep.
The fire is burning.
The bed is made.
You have a stolen stuffed toy in your pocket.
You have a stolen chocolate bar in your pocket.
You have the pliers from the generator.
You have the wire cutters from the store.

options.text: ENTER LAUNDROMAT: go into the laundromat and get {{Alice}} out of the rain.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s warm in here. You’ll feel better in no time.”

options.text: TALK TO PARKED ANDROID: ask one of the androids standing parked at the bus shelter where you could spend the night.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We need a place to stay… Do you know anywhere we could spend the night?” The android stands motionless and does not answer.

options.text: CHECK MOTEL: go over to the motel across the road.
CHECK PARKING LOT: go into the parking lot beside the motel.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} slip into the parking lot.

options.text: TALK TO ANDROID TRASH COLLECTOR: walk down to the other bus stop, by the garbage truck, where {{Alice}} can sit down.

I’m not so cold.” The android working at the garbage truck comes over: “You look lost.” {{Kara}}: “We have nowhere to go…” “I know someone who can help you.” He gives her an address. {{Kara}}: “But, that’s on the other side of town… We need a place for tonight! Come on, {{Alice}}.”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Look, the store is still open. Maybe we should go inside. At least you’ll be out of the cold.”

options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} stand in the rain.

options.outcome: The clothes inside are dry and still warm. {{Alice}}: “What are you doing? They’re not our clothes!” {{Kara}}: “We need them, {{Alice}}. You need something warm and I need to get rid of this uniform.” {{Alice}}: “But, that’s stealing! We can’t do that!”

options.outcome: They go back out into the rain.

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You’re right. We won’t do it, ok?” She closes the dryer.

options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the wire cutters back on the shelf.

options.text: USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION: ask {{Alice}} to knock over the cans, and take the cash from the register while the clerk sees to her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}, I need your help. You see those cans over there? I want you to go over and knock them down.” {{Alice}}: “Knock them down? But, why?” {{Kara}}: “Please. {{Alice}}, just trust me.” The cans crash to the floor and the clerk hurries over to {{Alice}}: “You all right? Are you hurt? Well, don’t worry, it’s just a few cans… They made a lot of noise, that’s all… Say, what’s a little girl like you doing out so late? It’s ok, I don’t bite… Cat got your tongue? Well, if you need anything, you just let me know, ok? And watch where you’re going, hm?”
options.successOutcome: Behind the checkout, {{Kara}} opens the register and takes the cash before he turns round. {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s go.” As the door closes behind them the clerk finds the register empty: “Fuck!” He runs out into the street, but they are gone. {{Kara}}: “We have some cash now…” {{Alice}}: “You used me to steal that money! How could you do that? I trusted you!”
options.failOutcome: {{Kara}} is still at the open register when he turns round.

options.text: USE GUN: send {{Alice}} outside and threaten the clerk with the gun.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Wait outside for me. I’ll just be two minutes.” {{Alice}}: “Wait outside? But, why?” {{Kara}}: “Please, {{Alice}}, just trust me.” When {{Alice}} has gone out, {{Kara}} points the gun at the clerk.

options.text: LEAVE SUPERMARKET: go back out into the street with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: They go back out into the rain.

options.text: NO: tell him you are all right.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “No, thanks. I’ll be all right…”

options.text: HELP: ask him for some money for a room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m with a little girl and we have nowhere to go… Could you spare some money so we can get a room for tonight?” Clerk: “Look, this is a convenience store, lady, not the Salvation Army… I can’t start handing out cash to every bum in the neighborhood.”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Sorry, but I have no choice.”

options.text: CALM: tell him to do what you say and all will be well.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Just do what I say and everything will be all right.”

options.text: STAY: hide the gun and let the customer pay and leave.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} lowers the gun out of sight: “Not a word.” The customer comes up to the checkout: “Excuse me… Are you done?” {{Kara}}: “Go ahead.” Clerk: “$4.95, please.” The customer pays and leaves without noticing anything.

options.text: BACK OFF!: order him to step back and take the money yourself.

options.text: TURN AROUND!: order him to turn around and take the money yourself.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Turn around! I’m sorry, but I really need this money.” She takes the cash from the register. Clerk: “Fuck!”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Put the cash on the counter.” The clerk reaches into the register and comes up with a pistol: “You better get outta here before things get nasty.”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You see that little girl outside? Her name is {{Alice}}. She’s nine years old and this is the worst night of her life. All I need is a few dollars so we can find a place for tonight. And I’m not leaving without that money.” The clerk lowers his pistol and hands her the money; he will not call the police.

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay, I’m going.” She backs out of the store without the money.

options.text: FACTUAL: tell her there was no other way.

options.text: JUSTIFY: tell her you needed the money.

options.text: UNCERTAIN: tell her it seemed like the right thing to do.

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I don’t know what the humans did to you, but she had nothing to do with it.” {{Ralph}}: “All humans want to hurt us… But {{Ralph}} won’t let them hurt him again… No, he won’t let them…”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We thought nobody was here… All we want is a place to spend the night.”

options.text: [GUN]: point the gun at him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Touch a hair on her head and I’ll kill you!” {{Ralph}}: “No, don’t hurt {{Ralph}}!”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Listen, we really need some help. It would be so kind of you, if you’d let us stay…”

options.text: LEAVE: tell him you are going.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay… We’re leaving… So you’ll be safe again… Come here, {{Alice}}.” They go back out through the fence to the street.

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I think we’d better go. Come on, {{Alice}}.” They go back out through the fence to the street.

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay. We’ll just stay the night.” {{Ralph}}: “Come on! Come! Come! Come on! This way! {{Ralph}} has lived here since he ran away... {{Ralph}} never goes outside, so no one knows he lives here... Humans come in to squat from time to time, but you know, {{Ralph}} just hides ’til they leave. Come on! You can make yourself at home here. {{Ralph}} is gonna go into the other room… He would like to stay with you… But he has things to do…” {{Kara}}: “It’s just for one night, {{Alice}}. We’ll find a better place tomorrow… Right… Let’s see where you can sleep…”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Sit down, and I’ll start a fire.” She takes the matches from the shelf by the fireplace, wood from beside the door and paper from next to the trash bin, and gets a fire going.

options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts together a bed for {{Alice}} by the fireplace out of what she can find in the house.

options.text: TALK TO {{RALPH}}: ask {{Ralph}} about the symbols he is carving into the wall.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: ““{{rA9}}”… What does that mean?” {{Ralph}}: “What?” {{Kara}}: “Those symbols… Why are you writing that?” {{Ralph}}: “I don’t know… I don’t know…”
options.fact: In the abandoned house, {{Ralph}} was carving the same symbols into the walls with his knife, over and over: “{{rA9}}”. When you asked what they mean, he said he did not know.
