options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} back out through the fence to the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s free-roam phase [FIND SHELTER FOR THE NIGHT] with all its branches as one repeatable scene: the street (ENTER LAUNDROMAT, TALK TO PARKED ANDROID, CHECK MOTEL, CHECK PARKING LOT, TALK TO ANDROID TRASH COLLECTOR, CHECK SQUAT, ENTER SUPERMARKET, in the chart’s order), the laundromat (INSPECT DRYER, then the template’s STEAL / DON’T STEAL, then WEAR CLOTHES or DISTURB MAN), the store (TALK TO CLERK with the template’s NO / HELP when Kara wears the stolen clothes, NOTICE CASH REGISTER, NOTICE CAN STACK, the three STEAL / LEAVE item pairs, USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION with STEAL DISCREETLY or TAKE TOO MUCH TIME, USE GUN with the template’s SINCERE / CALM / AGGRESSIVE, CASH REGISTER, CUSTOMER ARRIVES with STAY / LEAVE, BACK OFF! / TURN AROUND! / OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS!, CLERK GRABS A GUN with CONVINCE / GIVE UP, Alice’s “How did you get it?” with TRUTH / LIE and FACTUAL / JUSTIFY / UNCERTAIN / APOLOGIZE, and CLERK SPOTS {{KARA}} STEALING with [GUN] then ANGRY / APOLOGETIC / CALM and TAKE MONEY, or LEAVE or PUT BACK), the parking lot (BREAK INTO CAR with STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING, the pliers on the generator as TAKE WIRE CUTTERS, CUT PARKING LOT FENCE), and the squat (CUT STREET FENCE, MEET {{RALPH}} with the template’s ANDROID / LITTLE GIRL / INNOCENT / JUSTIFY, then [GUN] / INSIST / REASSURE / HOSPITALITY / LEAVE, then LEAVE / STAY, then START A FIRE, MAKE A BED, the template’s rA9 talk, LEAVE SQUAT and TALK TO {{ALICE}}). Every prompt is one visit of this scene offering only its buttons; buttons show the game’s label first and the spoken line is in the outcome. The chart groups INSIST, REASSURE and HOSPITALITY as CONVINCE, [GUN] as THREATEN WITH GUN, and the LEAVEs as GIVE UP and LEAVE SQUAT; BACK OFF! and TURN AROUND! are its “DON’T MOVE”, OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS! its OPEN CASH REGISTER, STAY / LEAVE at the customer its RESUME HOLD UP / GIVE UP, and STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING its STAY / FIND ANOTHER OPTION. Alice’s arrows (small 1, large 2), all the template’s: STEAL −1 (on choosing, whether or not the theft works), DON’T STEAL +1 (once), USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION −1 (on choosing), APOLOGIZE +1 (after the diversion, and after TRUTH), hold-up money without convincing −1 (Alice’s “How did you get it?”), CONVINCE +1 (the template’s automatic LIE), [GUN] when seen stealing −1 (one arrow; the wiki’s second for the register is not built, the template wins), STAY HERE −2. No other option moves anything. Gates: the gun from Stormy Night opens USE GUN, [GUN] at the checkout and [GUN] with Ralph, and closes HOSPITALITY (the template’s locks); USE GUN and the diversion follow NOTICE CASH REGISTER, and the diversion also needs NOTICE CAN STACK (the chart; the template words its lock as the can stack); the store’s wire cutters need the fence seen first (PowerPyx); the motel needs the stolen clothes and the register money (PowerPyx). Being caught is deterministic, as PowerPyx says: one item is safe, a second, on any visit, is always seen (the wiki’s “less likely” is not modelled as chance); without the gun Kara hands back everything she took from the store (wiki), and the store is closed to her after any robbery or attempt. Not built: patch 1.06 removed the third button after CLERK GRABS A GUN (SOURCES.md), so there is none. Simplifications: the template’s turned-away lines are the CHECK MOTEL outcome, and CHECK MOTEL is offered again only when Kara’s clothes or money have changed; the laundromat is not offered again once the clothes are worn or the man has woken; leaving the squat after meeting Ralph closes it (wiki); TALK TO PARKED ANDROID and WALK ON (the template’s “Going too far away”) are offered once. The trash collector is a street action (the template’s “Alice sits at the bus stop”); after 12 street actions without it, it is the only one left (PowerPyx: “You are forced to talk to Alice at some point”). {{ALICE}} TOO COLD (the wiki’s 12 minutes outside after the trash collector) is a budget of 12 street actions after the talk; time inside a building does not count, and once the budget is spent Kara’s next moment on the street ends the search. Risks: the laundromat QTE 0.2 and the register QTE 0.25 are unsourced (the chart shows a failure branch for each; no source gives a number). Breaking the car window and cutting the fence have no failure branch and no risk. Left out: the shop scans, the second washer, the motel mural, the window scope of the laundromat, and the gun, toy and pliers on the motel TV stand.

nodes.title: Something to read or watch
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}}, out of the rain for a moment.

situationWhen.text: On top of the cupboard next to the laundromat door, someone has left two magazines.
The television on the wall of the convenience store is showing the {{Channel16}} news.

media.title: Century: The Bee-Line to Disaster
facts: Century reports that pollinating bees are officially extinct: wild bees now exist only in captivity, after Colony Collapse Disorder was accelerated by pesticides, parasites and pollution. One in three mouthfuls of food relies on pollination, and famine could mean millions of deaths. {{CyberLife}}, with the agency that announced the extinction, plans to build robotic bees, and {{Detroit}} Urban Farms is trying modified strains of captive bees.

media.title: Gossips Weekly: It’s Time to Face the Music
facts: Gossips Weekly reports that for the younger generation, watching concerts in VR has become the norm; a music company has launched a campaign to bring back old-school concerts with live audiences, starting with the band Break the Wall, and next wants to bring back music festivals.

media.title: the {{Channel16}} news
facts: {{Channel16}} reports that the first {{CyberLife}} zoo in {{Detroit}} opened today: hundreds of species, most of them now extinct, recreated with android technology in more than 100 acres of natural environments, including polar bears, leopards, elephants and two blue whales. {{CyberLife}} has announced eleven new android zoos across the country.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chapter’s optional media, shown the first time {{Kara}} walks into each place: in the laundromat the two magazines on the cupboard by the door (READ “BEE-LINE TO DISASTER” and READ “FACE THE MUSIC”, Century #3 and Gossips Weekly #26), in the store the template’s “Watch TV” (the {{Channel16}} report on the android zoo). Facts are summarized from the wiki’s magazine pages and the template’s broadcast; the newsreader is not named. None of them changes public opinion. The old motel-television scene (R10b) is gone: the template puts this broadcast in the store, and no source has a television report in the motel in this chapter.

No arrow for sleeping beside her here: the wiki limits that up to the motel and the squat, and the car’s large down came with STAY HERE or {{ALICE}} TOO COLD.

nodes.title: Back to life
nodes.situation: NOV 6TH, 2038. AM 03:34. You are {{Markus}}. The last thing you remember is the police shooting you in {{Carl}}’s studio. Now your systems reboot. You are lying on your back in the rain, in a pit of broken androids: bodies, arms, heads and torn-out parts piled in the mud as far as you can see. Everything you see is red and broken by interference, and every sound reaches you muffled.
facts: You woke at 3:34 in the morning on 6 November 2038 in a landfill of broken androids, after the police shot you in {{Carl}}’s studio.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} lifts his head out of the mud.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s start node and checkpoint BACK TO LIFE. The date and time are the chapter’s own (“NOV 6TH, 2038”, “AM 03:34”). Both Broken endings end with the police shooting {{Markus}} (the engine’s Broken outcome), and the wiki and PowerPyx say this chapter plays the same either way, so nothing here depends on the earlier choice. The red filter with interference and the muffled sound are the wiki’s Notes on the damaged eye and audio processor. No stat change; the chapter has none.

nodes.title: Analyze self
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, lying in the mud of the landfill. You run a diagnosis on yourself, part by part. OPTICAL UNIT: Impaired vision. CORRUPTED MIND PALACE. AUDIO PROCESSOR: Corrupted audio data. DAMAGED. PUMP REGULATOR: All systems in LOW POWER MODE. DEFECTIVE. LEFT AND RIGHT LEG COMPONENTS: MISSING. Unable to stand.
facts: Your diagnosis in the landfill: optical unit impaired (corrupted), audio processor damaged, thirium pump regulator defective with all systems in low power mode, and both legs missing.

outcomes.0: Diagnosis complete. {{Markus}} cannot stand; he starts dragging himself through the mud on his arms.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANALYZE SELF: the template’s observation group “Diagnose”, its four readouts quoted in the game’s order and wording. In the game the player has to find the four spots on {{Markus}}’s body (PowerPyx; on Experienced they are not marked), all of them, in any order and with nothing to get wrong, so this is a narrated event rather than a choice of order. PowerPyx names the spots LED, audio processor, pump regulator and leg; the template’s readouts (optical unit, audio processor, pump regulator, legs) win (research note §10, discrepancy 4). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. No stat change.

nodes.title: Repair legs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, pulling yourself through the pit on your arms between the bodies. Legs lie torn off in the mud around you, and you examine them. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6847j. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6321t. Status: DAMAGED. INCOMPATIBLE. LEFT LEG COMPONENT #8427g. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE.
facts: You replaced your missing legs with a compatible right leg (#6847j) and left leg (#8427g) torn from other androids; a damaged right leg (#6321t) was incompatible.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} fits the right leg #6847j and the left leg #8427g, one after the other, and gets to his feet.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s REPAIR LEGS, with the template’s three leg readouts (observation groups “Compatible right leg”, “Incompatible right leg”, “Left leg”) in the game’s order and wording; the template’s #6321t is used, not the wiki’s #6312t. PowerPyx: “Follow the button prompts to repair the legs, nothing you can do wrong here”, so this is a narrated event with no risk. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hear about {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on your new legs, making your way through the pit. As you pass, an android stuck in the wall of bodies, so old and broken that you cannot tell what he was made for, grabs your arm and stares at you: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}! Find {{Jericho}}!..” As he holds you, something passes from him into your memory: a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}. Then he shuts down for good.
facts: In the landfill a dying android grabbed you and said: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}!” Before he shut down he passed you a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls free of the dead hand and goes on.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s event HEAR ABOUT JERICHO (the template’s section “Android grabs Markus”, speaker Phileas, whose line is quoted). The key: the Phileas page (“He carried a key to locate Jericho, which is copied to Markus and the latter uses it to find the freighter”) and the Jericho location page (“Phileas gave Markus a copy of his key to locate Jericho before permanently shutting down”); how it passes is not described, so it is narrated plainly. {{Markus}} does not learn the android’s name, so none is given. Sets fromDeadJerichoKey for Jericho (chapter 14). The old scene’s “single word” and “symbol” had no source and are gone. No stat change.

nodes.title: Passage of limbs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The only way out of the pit is a tight chasm between two walls of android bodies, and you squeeze into it. Hands of dying androids reach out of the walls, grab your arms and your legs and try to hold you down. A voice beside your head: “Where are you going?”
facts: Leaving the pit, you squeezed through a passage of dying androids whose hands grabbed you and tried to hold you down.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} tears free of the hands one after another and pushes through to the other side.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s PASSAGE OF LIMBS, with the template’s line (“Other android grabs Markus”: “Where are you going?”). PowerPyx: “a tight chasm Markus needs to squeeze through. There are hands of dying androids sticking out the side trying to hold Markus down. Press the button prompts here.” Neither the chart nor any source shows a failure branch, so there is no risk roll. No stat change.

nodes.title: Junkyard
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You come out into the open junkyard: a plain of broken androids under the rain and the floodlights, a crane swinging over the piles on the far left, a yellow neon sign reading VETA, and at the far end a slippery slope of bodies, the only way out. Many of the bodies still move. Some repeat the phrases they were made for, muffled in your damaged hearing: “An unexpected error has occurred. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.” “Don’t forget your dental appointment next Friday at 8 AM.” “Would you like another glass of red wine, Madam?” “Malfunction detected.” One keeps muttering: “I have to get to {{Jericho}}... Androids live in freedom there… I got to get to {{Jericho}}... No other choice…” Before you can climb out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts from the androids around you.
facts: In the junkyard, broken androids kept repeating their old service phrases, and one muttered that he had to get to {{Jericho}}, where androids live in freedom.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} starts searching the junkyard for parts.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint JUNKYARD (its image shows the crane and the yellow VETA sign; the wiki notes the sign in the final cutscene). The background lines are the template’s “Background dialogues”, which it lists as audible though not subtitled; four of them are quoted, plus the {{Jericho}} line, which the template keeps as audible (research note §10, discrepancy 6). The two TL400 lines and the others are left out. The objective is the wiki’s “Replace damaged parts” and PowerPyx’s “With all parts found (Optical Unit, Pump, Audio Processor) you can now climb the slippery slope”. No stat change.

nodes.title: Search for parts
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the open junkyard under the rain. To get out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts taken from the androids around you, then climb the slippery slope at the far end. You can search in any order, one thing at a time.

options.text: Pull out the android head sticking out of the wall of bodies on the far left, under the crane.
options.fact: In the junkyard you took your new optical unit, #8087q with a blue iris, from a talking AK700 head, after a crane dumped a load of bodies on you and you dug yourself out.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} pulls the head out of the wall. Its eyes open: “Hello. I’m an AK700 android. I was designed to serve you. What can I do for you?” Overhead the crane swings round and opens its grab, and a load of android bodies pours down on top of him. Buried, he digs and claws his way up through the bodies until he is out, the head still in his hand. He examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #8087q - BLUE IRIS. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. As he takes it out, the head speaks again: “My program has detected an anomaly. Please contact the nearest {{CyberLife}} maintenance center.” He replaces his damaged optical unit with it. The red haze and the interference clear, and he can scan his surroundings again.

options.text: Examine the optical unit of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An optical unit you examined in the junkyard (#9754h) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} kneels by the android and examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #9754h. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Go to the android lying motionless in the middle of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} crosses toward the middle of the junkyard, between androids lying in the mud.

options.text: Examine the thirium pump regulator of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: A pump regulator you examined in the junkyard (#9474) was low on energy and incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} opens the android’s chest and examines the regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #9474. Status: LOW ENERGY. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Take the pump regulator from the dead android near the slope.
options.fact: You took your new pump regulator (#2886) from a dead android near the slope of the junkyard.
options.outcome: Near the foot of the slope {{Markus}} kneels by a dead android and opens its chest: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He takes it out and replaces his own defective regulator. His systems come out of low power mode.

options.text: Search the head lying on the right side of the junkyard.
options.fact: You took your new audio processor (#4903) from a head on the right side of the junkyard.
options.outcome: On the right side of the area {{Markus}} finds the head and examines it: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4903. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He pulls out his own damaged audio processor and plugs in the new one. Sound crashes in: the rain, the wind, the droning of the storm and the voices of the broken androids, deafening after the silence.

options.text: Examine the audio processor of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An audio processor you examined in the junkyard (#4807) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} turns the android’s head and examines the processor behind its ear: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4807. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Climb the slippery slope at the far end of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} starts up the slope, sliding back on the loose bodies and pulling himself up again, handhold after handhold.

situationWhen.text: Your optical unit is still impaired: everything is red and broken by interference, and you cannot scan your surroundings.
Your new blue optical unit works: your vision is clear and you can scan your surroundings.
Your audio processor is still damaged; the rain and the voices reach you muffled.
Your new audio processor works; the storm is deafening.
Your thirium pump regulator is still defective, and all your systems are in low power mode.
Your new pump regulator works.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. You will need another compatible one, and without scanning you have not found one yet.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. Scanning, you find another compatible one in a dead android near the slope.
All three parts are replaced. Nothing holds you here.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket [ SEARCH FOR PARTS ] as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet, in any order (PowerPyx: the parts can be found in any order; the chart draws no edge between its branches). Chart nodes here: FIND OPTICAL UNIT with CRANE DUMPS BODIES and DIG YOURSELF OUT as one option, because they always happen together (PowerPyx: interacting with the head “brings a lot of dead androids falling down from a crane”; digging out “gets you the Optical Unit”); the eye comes from the talking AK700 head, as in the template (“Take head”, “Remove optical unit”, with its two lines), and is #8087q with a blue iris; FIND AUDIO PROCESSOR (#4903; PowerPyx “in a head on the right side of the area”, while the wiki’s Biocomponent 4903 page has it in an android’s hand); FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID (#2886, only after sparing the android in the middle, and only once the new eye can scan: PowerPyx “You can scan the area and find another one near the slope”); and CLIMB SLOPE, which ends the scene and needs all three parts. Going to the middle of the junkyard plays ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID, the next two scenes, which then come back here. The three incompatible readouts of the template’s “Search for components” group (#9754h, #9474, #4807) are optional looks (PUMP REGULATOR without the word thirium, as in the earlier scenes); the model names the wiki gives for their androids are not in the game’s text and are left out. Departures: in the game {{Markus}} can miss the crawling android and can take the dead android’s regulator without ever finding the living one (PowerPyx “or you never found it in the first place”); here both encounters happen together on the way to the middle, in the template’s order, and the dead android’s regulator is offered only after sparing her, so both choices are always presented (as in the previous version). The wiki’s note that the begging android must be met “before replacing Markus’ damaged parts” is not applied: PowerPyx’s own route meets him right after finding the optical unit (research note §8, question 3). Left out (not in the template, not on the chart): the singing android and the grappling android. No risk, no stat change: the chapter has no failure node and no arrow.

nodes.title: Android begs to die
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, crossing toward the middle of the junkyard. An android is crawling through the mud at your feet, too broken to get up. As you step past him he grabs your leg and holds on: “I’m begging you, please… End it… I don’t wanna live anymore…”

options.text: KILL: reach into his chest and pull out his thirium pump.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life, and you did: you pulled out his thirium pump and he shut down.

options.text: SPARE: pull your leg free and leave him.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life. You refused and left him there, begging you not to leave him.

outcomes.0: “Make it quick…” {{Markus}} kneels, reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out his thirium pump. The android shuts down in the mud.
outcomes.1: “No, please… Don’t leave me!.. Don’t leave me!” {{Markus}} pulls his leg free and walks on. The android is left alive in the mud behind him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL / KILL. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Android begs to die”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; the plea and the two replies are the template’s lines. The android is male (the wiki’s Sorrowful Android: “the android grabs Markus on the leg”; KILL: “Markus takes out the android’s heart”; SPARE: “he will beg Markus not to leave him though alas he is left alive”). In the game he is optional and easy to miss (PowerPyx); here he is always met on the way to the middle of the junkyard (see the previous scene’s note). Neither option gives {{Markus}} a part. Records fromDeadBeggar (Kill or Refuse to kill). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

nodes.title: The pump regulator
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the middle of the junkyard, a few steps from the crawling android. An android lies motionless in the mud with her chest open, and you examine her regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. You reach in to take it. She wakes, and her hand closes on your arm: “Wait! Please! Please, don’t do that! I wanna live…”

options.text: KILL: pull out her pump regulator and take it.
options.fact: The pump regulator you run on came from a living android in the junkyard who begged you to let her live; you took it and she shut down.

options.text: SPARE: leave her the regulator and look for another one.
options.fact: In the junkyard an android whose pump regulator you needed begged to live, and you spared her.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls the regulator from her chest. She says nothing more; she slowly shuts down. He replaces his own defective regulator with hers, and his systems come out of low power mode.
outcomes.1: “Thank you…” {{Markus}} lets go of the regulator and stands up. He will have to find another compatible one.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL FOR PUMP / KILL FOR PUMP. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Try to take pump regulator from android”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; her plea and “Thank you…” are the template’s lines, and KILL has none (the template’s ø). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. The compatible readout #2886 is the template’s (it does not say which android carries it, so the dead android near the slope shows the same part number). She is female (the wiki’s Begging Android; the Markus page: “He gets a choice to kill or spare her”). The old scene’s “you have minutes” is gone: no source gives a timer. After SPARE, the dead android’s regulator near the slope is the way (PowerPyx), back in the search. Records fromDeadPump (Kill for pump or Refuse to kill for pump), and after KILL fromDeadPumpSource (Living android). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

nodes.title: {{Markus}} came back from the dead
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You haul yourself over the top of the slope and stand. Behind you the landfill stretches away under the rain, the floodlights and the yellow VETA sign; ahead are the lights of the city. You raise a hand to your temple and pull out your LED, the light that marks you as an android. Without it, nobody will know what you are. You think of the dying android’s words: there is a place where androids can be free.
facts: You climbed out of the landfill and pulled the LED from your temple, so you now pass for human. Your right eye is now blue (#8087q). You set off for the city to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} walks away from the landfill toward the city. “My name is {{Markus}}.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending MARKUS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD, the chapter’s only outcome (wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”), reached on every path. PowerPyx: “After Markus reaches the top of the slope he must still remove his LED (to appear like a human). Then he walks away”; the Markus page: “his right eye has been exchanged for a blue eye (#8087q)”. The closing line is the template’s spoken “My name is Markus.”; the line before it, “Markus.”, is marked unused in the template and is not built. The jacket the Markus page says he steals on the way to the city is not in this chapter’s text and is left to Jericho. Records fromDeadOutcome (Markus came back from the dead) and fromDeadLedRemoved. No stat change.

nodes.title: In the zen garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is November 6th, 2038, 9:56 in the morning. You close your eyes and enter the zen garden, the virtual space where you report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}. A pond lies in front of you, with paths running left and right along its edges and bridges leading out to an island in the middle.
facts: You report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}, in the zen garden, a virtual space you enter in your mind.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} looks around the garden.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint IN THE ZEN GARDEN (date and time from the template’s notes: NOV 6TH, 2038, AM 09:56). A narrated event with a single Continue. The engine also records here, once, what this chapter reads from earlier chapters (deviant found in Partners, the spilled drink and the statuette there; confession, death and intervention in The Interrogation; {{Kara}} and {{Todd}} after Stormy Night; {{Carl}} after Broken), so every later scene reads the same snapshot. No stat change.

nodes.title: The zen garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the zen garden. A path runs left along the edge of the pond toward a circular archway; another runs right along the water. On the island in the middle of the pond, {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.

situationWhen.text: Off the path to the right, a smaller path leads to a small graveyard.

options.text: Cross the bridge to the island where {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} crosses the bridge to the island. {{Amanda}} is among her roses.

options.text: Go left along the pond to the circular archway and examine the stone there.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the edge of the pond to the circular archway on the left of the path and examines the stone inside it.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There is one.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: one gravestone, for the {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There are two.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: two gravestones, one for each {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND AMANDA with its two optional side branches, as a repeatable scene: FIND MAGIC STONE (PowerPyx: “go left along the edge of the pond until you find a circular archway… Interact with it”) and CHECK THE GRAVES (wiki: “only if Connor previously died in The Hostage and/or The Interrogation”; the Zen Garden page: “gravestones for killed Connor models”). Neither has a line, a clue text or a stat change in the template; no source describes the stone, so the outcome says only that {{Connor}} examines it. The graveyard shows one gravestone per earlier {{Connor}} death (the benchmark’s reading of “Another gravestone is present” on The Interrogation page). Crossing to the island ends the scene.

nodes.title: Talk with {{Amanda}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the island in the zen garden. “Hello, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}… It’s good to see you.”

situationWhen.text: {{Amanda}}: “I expected you to find the deviant who killed that man… I must admit I’m a little bit disappointed...” You: “I’m sorry. I know I should have succeeded.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll show more foresight in the future.”

{{Amanda}}: “Congratulations, {{Connor}}... Finding that deviant was far from easy, and the way you interrogated it was very clever. You’ve been remarkably efficient, {{Connor}}.” You: “Thank you, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “We’ve asked the police department to transfer it to us for further study. It may teach us something about what happened.”

{{Amanda}}: “Your predecessor was unfortunately destroyed... It knew deviants could be unpredictable, but it wasn’t careful enough… I hope you won’t make the same mistake.” You: “I don’t intend to.” {{Amanda}}: “When a {{Connor}} model is destroyed, its memory is transferred to the next one, but some data can be lost in the process. Avoid being destroyed. It will be better for you and the investigation…” You: “I understand.”

{{Amanda}}: “Finding that deviant was far from easy… you showed great skill in your investigation. But you knew deviants could be unstable. You should have been more cautious.” You: “I thought I could make it talk… It was a judgement error.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll be more careful in future.”

outcomes.0: {{Amanda}} turns from her roses to {{Connor}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK WITH AMANDA, opening: one of four reactions, decided by Partners and The Interrogation, each with the template’s Amanda arrow, applied by the engine here: deviant not found in Partners, large down (−2); “Got a confession, without dying”, large up (+2); “Connor died during The Interrogation”, small down (−1); found but no confession, small down (−1). The wiki’s chapter page and Relationship Stat page list the same four. A confession followed by a death counts as a death (the template’s confession variant reads “without dying”). “The DPD” is rendered as “the police department”. The cut line about the transfer request (“We hope they’ll accept our request…”) is not built.

nodes.title: What {{Connor}} thought of the deviant
nodes.whenNot: Connor never found the deviant in Partners, so Amanda does not ask about the interrogation.
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} among the roses. {{Amanda}}: “The interrogation seemed… challenging… What did you think of the deviant?”

options.text: TRAUMATIZED: say it showed signs of trauma after being abused by its owner.
options.outcome: “It showed signs of PTSD after being abused by its owner, as if its original program had been completely replaced by new instructions.”

options.text: {{DEVIANCY}}: say it showed every sign of deviancy and the model was clearly defective.
options.outcome: “It showed all the signs of deviancy: cognitive instability, unpredictable behavior, and the emulation of human emotions. It was even afraid to die. The model was clearly defective.”

options.text: INTERVENTION: say you kept it from being damaged, so it can still be analyzed.
options.outcome: “I prevented it from being damaged, so we might still learn something by analyzing it.”

options.text: REGRETS: say the previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger.
options.outcome: “It could’ve killed everyone in the room. The previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger. It was a mistake to let an armed policeman so close to the deviant.”

options.text: SIMULATION: say it simulated human emotion, fear above all, very convincingly.
options.outcome: “It simulated human emotion, fear in particular, in a very convincing way. It seemed completely overwhelmed by them, and behaved irrationally…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The first of {{Amanda}}’s three questions, asked only if the deviant was found in Partners (the template nests it in that variant). Buttons in the game’s order: TRAUMATIZED, DEVIANCY, INTERVENTION (unlocked by “Intervened and saved the deviant in The Interrogation”; if he also confessed, {{Connor}} adds “It said something to me: ‘The truth is inside’…”), REGRETS (unlocked by {{Connor}}’s death in The Interrogation) and SIMULATION (its cut ending, “as a human would under extreme stress”, is not built). No arrow on any answer (template; PowerPyx “No effect”).

nodes.title: What {{Connor}} makes of {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} in the zen garden. {{Amanda}}: “This… Lieutenant {{Anderson}} has been officially assigned to the deviancy case… What do you make of him?”

options.text: UNPLEASANT: call him unpleasant and unprofessional.
options.outcome: “I find him unpleasant and unprofessional. He seems to have an addictive personality, has a lack of respect for procedure, and despises androids - which makes our relationship difficult.”

options.text: DYSFUNCTIONAL: call him dysfunctional, with a personal situation affecting his work.
options.outcome: “I would define him as ‘dysfunctional’. He obviously has a personal situation impacting his professional behavior and... seems to have no interest in the investigation.”

nodes.title: Arrive at the police station
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, back in your body, in the reception hall of the {{Detroit}} police station. People wait on the seats. A woman: “I’m getting nervous, Mark.” The man with her: “It’s okay… Just tell ’em what happened to you.” “But it was all over so quickly... I didn’t even see his face!” Near a television, another woman hands a shaken man a cup of water. Gates bar the way into the station, and an android receptionist is at the desk. If you try the gates without signing in, an android stops you: “No access without prior authorization.”
facts: At the station reception you were told that Lieutenant {{Anderson}} had not arrived yet and that you could wait at his desk.

media.title: the news at reception
facts: The news at the station reception: a Russian carrier and an American patrol boat clashed in the Arctic last night and exchanged warning shots, apparently with no damage or casualties. The Minister for Defense spoke of “intolerable provocation that cannot go unanswered”; the countries in the region have called for military forces to withdraw and for an international conference. Neither Moscow nor Washington has responded.

options.text: Research Lt. {{ANDERSON}} on the terminal.
options.fact: Research Lt. {{Anderson}}. “{{DETROIT}} POLICE DISMANTLE A NETWORK OF {{REDICE}} DEALERS”. February 3rd, 2028. More than 50 arrests throughout the country. {{Detroit}}’s finest has dealt a massive blow to the city’s growing {{RedIce}} epidemic, with a number of high-profile dealers and suppliers now behind bars and narcotics seized with a street value of $500,000. Detective {{Hank}} {{Anderson}}, a young but hugely talented Detective, is said to have been instrumental in the operation, which took months of planning. The DA described the work of Detective {{Anderson}} and his colleagues as “model investigative police work”. “DETECTIVE {{ANDERSON}} PROMOTED TO THE RANK OF LIEUTENANT”. August 22nd, 2029. Becoming the youngest lieutenant on the {{Detroit}} police force. Lieutenant {{Hank}} {{Anderson}} was among the most decorated Detectives in the police department’s recent history, securing a number of high-profile arrests and serving as an integral member of the force. Captain {{Fowler}} said the promotion was “long over-due”, describing {{Anderson}} as “among the most talented police I’ve ever worked with”. The new Lieutenant is expected to rise quickly through the ranks of the department and is already being tipped as a future Commissioner. “NEW RECORD SEIZURE OF {{REDICE}} IN {{DETROIT}}!” November 23rd, 2031. Nearly a ton of {{RedIce}} discovered in the hold of a boat after a long investigation conducted by Lieutenant {{Anderson}} of the {{Detroit}} police force.

ANDERSON, then the [ WAIT FOR HANK ] block before he arrives, as one repeatable scene: EXPLORE THE STATION (PowerPyx: “At Hank’s desk, sit in the chair in front of it briefly, then get up again”), EXAMINE HANK’S DESK and LEARN ABOUT HANK. Anderson” (the three articles, offered once a desk item has been scanned, since LEARN ABOUT HANK follows EXAMINE HANK’S DESK on the chart). The nameplate, tissue and police-cases strings in the string table are not placed by the template and are not built. The headset, cap, stickers and hairs unlock {{Connor}}’s MUSIC, BASKETBALL, ANTI-ANDROIDS and DOG topics later. Also here, with no stat change: Officer {{Wilson}} (“Finding Hank’s desk”), Officer {{Chris}} (the template’s three variants), the call to {{Hank}} with the game’s LEAVE A MESSAGE / HANG UP buttons (calling at all is optional, as in the game), the man in the holding cell, and, only if the android was sent back to his cell in The Interrogation, TALK WITH CARLOS’ ANDROID, which plays the two cell scenes that follow. The scene ends either by going to the break room (TALK WITH GAVIN and the break-room TV) or by sitting down to wait; either way {{Hank}} arrives next. These two exits are listed first, as in the other repeatable scenes of this chapter the main line comes first. The background chatter is quoted once; {{Wilson}}’s private phone call is not built; the magazines are a media scene after this one.

nodes.title: The magazines by {{Hank}}’s desk and the break-room TV
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, waiting for {{Hank}}. On a desk in the middle of the station, near his, lies a magazine.

situationWhen.text: In the break room you just left, the television is running the news.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: {{Ivanoff}} Says “Niet”!
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “{{Ivanoff}} Says ‘Niet’!”: after President {{Warren}} demanded that “all Russian troops withdraw from the arctic immediately”, the Russian president called her comments “megaphone diplomacy” and said “US sabre-rattling is the number one threat to stability in the region.” The Kremlin set out Russia’s claim to the territory in a detailed statement, and he would “remind President {{Warren}}” that “the United States is subject to UN conventions, like everybody else.” The conflict shows no signs of abating. On the cover: {{CyberLife}} is the world’s first trillion-dollar company; the global population has reached 10 billion.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Famous Painter Dies
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “Famous {{Detroit}} Painter Dies”: the death of the artist {{Carl}} {{Manfred}} is confirmed; the coroner described a “fatal cardiac event” induced by a stressful domestic situation, and his son {{Leo}} has asked the media to respect the family’s privacy. {{Carl}} rose to fame in the 2020s as a figurehead of neo-symbolism, went through a dark period marked by alcohol and drugs, and had returned to work in recent months. The Governor called him “one of {{Detroit}}’s brightest lights”; his estate will auction a collection of his paintings. On the cover: the UN warns of World War Three; President {{Warren}} is at 33% approval.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: The Three Laws of Robotic Parenting
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “The Three Laws of Robotic Parenting”: {{CyberLife}}’s child androids, once doubted, are now among its bestsellers: “Customizable, removable LED, no hunger, no expensive childcare... no smelly diapers!” With unemployment at 37.3%, $7,500 for a child that skips the teenage years and college looks like a wise investment against $350,000 over 17 years. A sociologist warns that these androids are leading fewer parents to have children when birthrates are already far too low (“the baby doom”); {{CyberLife}}’s director of humanization calls this “the usual resistance to new ideas” and the androids “a triumph of humanization design”. On the cover: the UN warns of World War Three; President {{Warren}} is at 33% approval.

media.title: the break-room news
facts: The break-room news: several sources report that {{CyberLife}} has provided the {{Detroit}} police with a prototype detective android. Police assistant androids have existed for several years, but this would be the first case of an android authorized to play an active role in criminal investigations; no one at {{CyberLife}} was available to comment.

Then the next report: the first book written by an artificial intelligence, “Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?”, has shot to the top of the bestseller list, and critics are unanimous in their praise. Designed by {{CyberLife}}, the AI known as VOLTAIRE analyzed human centers of interest on social networks for several months before its algorithms generated the plot; according to several specialists, most books written in the coming years will be the work of artificial intelligence.

media.title: the break-room news
facts: The break-room news: the police found the body of thirty-year-old {{CarlosOrtiz}} in his home last night, after calls from concerned neighbors. Known to the police as a petty criminal, he is reported to have suffered from a psychiatric condition and rarely left his apartment; he is thought to have died several weeks ago. The police appear to be treating the death as a homicide. His android is also reported missing.

Then the next report: the first book written by an artificial intelligence, “Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?”, has shot to the top of the bestseller list, and critics are unanimous in their praise. Designed by {{CyberLife}}, the AI known as VOLTAIRE analyzed human centers of interest on social networks for several months before its algorithms generated the plot; according to several specialists, most books written in the coming years will be the work of artificial intelligence.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s READ “IVANOFF SAYS “NIET”!” (always), READ “FAMOUS PAINTER DIES” (only if {{Carl}} died in Broken) and READ “ROBOTIC PARENTING” (only if he lived), on the counter near {{Hank}}’s desk (PowerPyx), with the break-room TV, which is offered only after {{Gavin}}. nodes.title: {{Hank}} storms out
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}.

situationWhen.text: Through the glass you hear Captain {{Fowler}}: “I’ve got ten new cases involving androids on my desk every day. We’ve always had isolated incidents, old ladies losing their android maids and that kind of crap… But now, we’re getting reports of assaults and even homicides, like that guy last night… This isn’t just {{CyberLife}}’s problem anymore. It’s now a criminal investigation and we’ve gotta deal with it before the shit hits the fan. I want you to investigate these cases and see if there’s any link.” {{Hank}}: “Why me? Why do I gotta be the one to deal with this shit? I am the least qualified cop in the country to handle this case! I know jack shit about androids, {{Jeffrey}}! I can barely change the settings on my own phone…” {{Fowler}}: “Everybody’s overloaded. I think you’re perfectly qualified for this type of investigation.” “Bullshit! The truth is nobody wants to investigate these fuckin’ androids and you left me holdin’ the bag!” “{{CyberLife}} sent over this android to help with the investigation. It’s a state-of-the-art prototype. It’ll act as your partner.” “No fuckin’ way! I don’t need a partner, and certainly not this plastic prick!” “{{Hank}}, you are seriously starting to piss me off! You are a police lieutenant, you are supposed to do what I say and shut your goddamn mouth!” “You know what my goddamn mouth has to say to you, huh?” “Ok, ok... I’ll pretend like I didn’t hear that, so I don’t have to add any more pages to your disciplinary folder ‘cause it already looks like a fuckin’ novel! This conversation is over!” “{{Jeffrey}}, Jesus Christ! Why are you doin’ this to me? You know how much I hate these fuckin’ things. Why you doin’ this to me?” “Listen, I’ve had just about enough of your bitching. Either you do your job or you hand in your badge. Now if you’ll excuse me, I’ve got work to do.”
From the desk you can see {{Hank}} and Captain {{Fowler}} arguing behind the glass, but you cannot hear them.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} storms out of the office and back to his desk.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK STORMS OUT, on the track that runs beside the [ WAIT FOR HANK ] block. If {{Connor}} followed, the template’s “Entering and listening” argument is quoted: {{Fowler}} assigns {{Hank}} the android cases with {{Connor}} as his partner. That it cannot be heard from the desk is the benchmark’s reading. No stat change.

nodes.title: Alone with Captain {{Fowler}}
nodes.whenNot: Connor did not follow Hank into Fowler’s office.
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in Captain {{Fowler}}’s office. {{Hank}} has just stormed out, and {{Fowler}} has turned back to his work.

options.text: {{ANDERSON}}: wonder aloud whether Lieutenant {{Anderson}} is the best person for this investigation.
options.outcome: “I wonder whether Lieutenant {{Anderson}} is really the best person for this investigation.” {{Fowler}}: “Hey, I don’t need a machine to tell me how to handle my men, okay? So get the fuck outta my office.” “Have a nice day, Captain.”

options.text: POSITIVE: say you are very pleased to have joined the team.
options.outcome: “I’m very pleased to have joined the team. I can assure you I’ll do my very best-” {{Fowler}}: “Close the door on your way out.” “Have a nice day, Captain.”

options.text: FILE: say you would like to start reviewing the case files.
options.outcome: “I would like to start reviewing the case files. Can you tell me where I-” {{Fowler}}: “Talk to {{Hank}}. Close the door on your way out.” “Have a nice day, Captain.”

options.text: LEAVE: say you will not keep him any longer.
options.outcome: “Well, then… I won’t keep you any longer. Have a nice day, Captain.”

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Connor}} alone with {{Fowler}} after {{Hank}} storms out, only if {{Connor}} followed. Buttons and lines from the template. No stat change (PowerPyx: “All responses to the Captain have no effect”).

nodes.title: Talk to {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Hank}}’s desk. He has dropped into his chair and is pointedly ignoring you.

options.text: NEW {{CONNOR}}: say you understand the destruction of your predecessor may have been unpleasant for him.
options.outcome: “I understand the destruction of my predecessor may have been unpleasant for you, Lieutenant. I’ll do everything I can to make sure it doesn’t happen again.”

options.text: LAST NIGHT: apologize for bothering him at the bar last night.
options.outcome: “I’m… sorry I bothered you at the bar last night, Lieutenant. I guess I ruined your evening…”

options.text: UNDERSTANDING: say you are sorry your presence inconveniences him.
options.outcome: “I get the impression my presence causes you some inconvenience, Lieutenant. I’d like you to know I’m very sorry about that.”

options.text: PRAGMATIC: say you know he does not like you, but you will both have to make an effort.
options.outcome: “Listen, I know you don’t like me, but we’re going to have to work together, we’ll both have to make an effort.”

options.text: CONSTRUCTIVE: say it is an honor to work with him.
options.outcome: “It’s an honor to be working with you, Lieutenant. I’m sure we’ll make a great team.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO HANK, first prompt (the template’s “Checking on Hank”). NEW CONNOR is unlocked by {{Connor}}’s death in The Interrogation; LAST NIGHT by “Spilled Hank’s drink in Partners” (the template’s only condition; the wiki adds that the deviant was not found, which the benchmark does not require). The template gives {{Hank}} no reply and no arrow on any of these.

nodes.title: Somewhere to sit
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Hank}}’s desk. He still has not looked up.

options.text: PARTNERS: say that now you are partners, it would be good to get to know each other.
options.outcome: “Now that we’re partners, it would be great to get to know each other better.” {{Connor}} takes the empty desk facing {{Hank}}’s.

options.text: POSITIVE: say you are very happy to be working with him.
options.outcome: “In any case, I’d like you to know I’m very happy to be working with you. I’m sure we’ll make a great team.” {{Connor}} takes the empty desk facing {{Hank}}’s.

options.text: DESK: ask whether there is a desk you could use.
options.outcome: “Is there a desk anywhere I could use?” {{Hank}}: “No one’s using that one.” {{Connor}} takes the empty desk facing {{Hank}}’s.

nodes.adaptationNote: The second prompt of TALK TO HANK. Buttons and lines from the template; no arrow. The template’s fourth button, THANKS, is cut content (marked unused; the wiki calls it permanently locked by a bug) and is not built. {{Connor}} sits at the spare desk after every answer (the {{Hank}} page: “Hank will gesture to sit at the empty desk across from him”).

nodes.title: Getting to know {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the empty desk facing {{Hank}}’s. He is at his terminal and plainly not in the mood to talk. You can make conversation, or ask to start on the case.

options.text: DOG: ask whether he has a dog.
options.outcome: “You have a dog, right?” {{Hank}}: “How do you know that?” “The dog hairs on your chair. I like dogs. What’s your dog’s name?” “What’s it to you? {{Sumo}}, I call him {{Sumo}}.”

options.text: BASKETBALL: ask whether he saw last night’s Gears game.
options.outcome: “You’re a {{Detroit}} Gears fan, right? Denton Carter scored 53% of his shots from the three-point line yesterday. Did you see the game?” {{Hank}}: “That’s what I was watchin’ at the bar last night.” “Oh…”

options.text: MUSIC: ask whether he listens to Knights of the Black Death.
options.outcome: “Do you listen to Knights of the Black Death? I really like that music. It’s… full of energy…” {{Hank}}: “You listen to Heavy Metal?” “Well, I don’t really listen to music, as such… but I’d like to.”

options.text: ANTI-ANDROIDS: ask whether there is a particular reason he despises you.
options.outcome: “A lot of people don’t appreciate having androids around… I was wondering… Is there any reason in particular you despise me?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah... there is one.”

options.text: {{FOWLER}}: ask whether he has known Captain {{Fowler}} long.
options.outcome: “Have you known Captain {{Fowler}} for long?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah... Too long.”

options.text: HOURS: ask whether he always arrives at this time.
options.outcome: “I was wondering… Do you always arrive at the office at this time?” {{Hank}}: “I arrive when I arrive. Stop busting my balls, okay?”

options.text: START WORKING: ask to see his files on deviants.
options.outcome: “If you have any files on deviants, I’d like to take a look at them…” {{Hank}}: “Terminal’s on your desk. Knock yourself out.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s LEARN ABOUT HANK topics, asked from the spare desk, as a repeatable scene until START WORKING (PowerPyx: “Additional questions will present themselves as you get answers”; Relationship Stat: “two increases possible”). Each topic can be asked once. DOG needs the hairs scanned, BASKETBALL the cap, MUSIC the headset, ANTI-ANDROIDS the stickers (template locks). Arrows from the template: DOG Hank small up (+1; {{Connor}} learns {{Sumo}}’s name, which Russian Roulette reads), BASKETBALL small down (−1), MUSIC small up (+1), ANTI-ANDROIDS small down (−1); FOWLER, HOURS and START WORKING none. The cut HANK’S SON topic and the cut photo of {{Cole}} are not built.

nodes.title: The case files
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the terminal on your desk, going through the files on deviants: “243 files… The first dates back nine months… It all started in {{Detroit}}… And quickly spread across the country…” Six reports are assigned to Lieutenant {{Anderson}}. Across from you, {{Hank}} is reading something on his tablet.

options.text: Tell {{Hank}} where you think the investigation should start.
options.outcome: “An AX400 is reported to have assaulted a man last night. That could be a good starting point for our investigation.” {{Hank}}, reading his tablet: “Uh, Jesus…”

options.text: Tell {{Hank}} where you think the investigation should start.
options.outcome: “An AX400 is reported to have murdered a man last night. That could be a good starting point for our investigation.” {{Hank}}, reading his tablet: “Uh, Jesus…”

options.text: Tell {{Hank}} where you think the investigation should start.
options.outcome: “We could follow up on one of these cases. See if we could figure out what happened. That might be a good way to start the investigation. What do you think?” {{Hank}}, reading his tablet: “Uh, Jesus…”

options.text: Open case file 01: a disappearance, still open.
options.fact: Case file 01 (disappearance, open, 10/04/38): a man left his android at home when he went to work; when he came back it was gone, with no trace of a break-in. The android may have left without being ordered to.
options.outcome: CASE FILE 01. DISAPPEARANCE. Victim: Gordon Lopez. Open. Offense: 10/04/38. “The plaintiff reports that he left his android at home as usual when he went to work. When he returned, the android was nowhere to be found. No trace of a break-in in the apartment. The android may have left the home without being ordered to.”

options.text: Open case file 02: an attack, still open.
options.fact: Case file 02 (attack, open, 09/14/38): an AV500 waiter at the FAST CONEY DOGS restaurant at 842 Chamberlain Avenue lunged at a customer and tried to strangle him, then left; it remains at large.
options.outcome: CASE FILE 02. ATTACK. Victim: Charles Bell. Open. Offense: 09/14/38, reported 09/15/38. “The plaintiff claims to have been attacked by a AV500 #234 777 821 model android working as a waiter in the FAST CONEY DOGS restaurant chain situated at 842 Chamberlain Avenue. The plaintiff claims the android ‘lunged’ at him unexpectedly and attempted to strangle the man, before leaving the scene. The android remains at large.”

options.text: Open case file 03: an attack, still open.
options.fact: Case file 03 (attack, open, 10/22/38): a woman was attacked by her AP700, which trashed several rooms of the house and fled.
options.outcome: CASE FILE 03. ATTACK. Victim: Sarah Cornwal. Open. Offense: 10/22/38, reported 10/23/38. “The plaintiff claims to have been attacked by her android, an AP700 #480 913 802 model. The android also trashed several rooms in the house before taking flight.”

options.text: Open case file 04: a disappearance, still open.
options.fact: Case file 04 (disappearance, open, 10/04/38): the manager of the EDEN CLUB reported that a WR400 sex android went home with a customer and never came back.
options.outcome: CASE FILE 04. DISAPPEARANCE. Victim: Floyd Mills. Open. options.outcome: CASE FILE 05. ATTEMPTED MURDER. Victim: {{LEO}} {{MANFRED}}. Solved. Offense: 11/05/38. “Famous painter {{Carl}} {{MANFRED}} was found dead in his home following an altercation between his android and his son. The latter’s witness statement attests to the android behaving violently. The android is thought to be a prototype (unknown model and serial number) and was destroyed at the scene by attending officers.” There is no picture of the android.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s EXAMINE FILES, as a repeatable scene: the template’s six case files (“Case 1” to “Case 6”), each read once, in any order, with the in-game report text; reference, victim, status and dates from the string table. File 05 ({{Markus}}’s, with no picture) follows {{Carl}}’s fate in Broken, and file 06 ({{Kara}}’s) follows {{Todd}}’s in Stormy Night (template variants). {{Todd}}’s surname is left out. {{Connor}}’s conclusion ends the scene, in the template’s three variants: an AX400 “assaulted” a man ({{Kara}} alive, {{Todd}} alive), “murdered” a man ({{Todd}} killed), or the generic “We could follow up on one of these cases” ({{Kara}} died in Stormy Night). Whether every file must be opened before the conclusion is not documented; here {{Connor}} can conclude at any time (the conclusion is listed first, the files after it). Which files were read is kept for later chapters. No stat change.

nodes.title: Talk about the case
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the spare desk. {{Hank}} keeps reading his tablet and makes no move to start on anything. You try again to get him to work the case.

options.text: DIRECT: tell him not to let his personal situation hamper the investigation.
options.outcome: “You shouldn’t let your personal situation hamper the investigation, Lieutenant.” {{Hank}}: “You don’t know what the hell you’re talking about. So why don’t you just run your program and shut the fuck up?”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: tell him to ask to be relieved if the situation does not suit him.
options.outcome: “If the situation doesn’t suit you, Lieutenant, you should ask to be relieved of duties and let me work with someone else.” {{Hank}}: “I know exactly what I have to do! So keep your advice to yourself and mind your own business! Fuckin’...”

options.text: PROFESSIONAL: say you know he did not ask for this, but you are sure he is a professional.
options.outcome: “I know you didn’t ask for this investigation, Lieutenant, but I’m sure you’re a professional.” {{Hank}}: “Why don’t you go fuck yourself?”

options.text: UNDERSTANDING: say you understand his personal issues, but he needs to move past them.
options.outcome: “I understand you’re facing personal issues, Lieutenant, but you need to move past them... and-” {{Hank}}: “Hey! Don’t talk to me like you know me. I’m not your friend and I don’t need your advice, okay?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK ABOUT THE CASE. Buttons and replies from the template; no arrow (PowerPyx: “All responses have no effect”).

nodes.title: {{Hank}} is mad
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} has turned on you, furious. You can say one more thing.

options.text: DETERMINED: say you were assigned this mission and did not come to wait until he feels like working.
options.outcome: “I’ve been assigned this mission, Lieutenant. I didn’t come here to wait until you feel like working.” {{Hank}} grabs {{Connor}} by the collar and shoves him against the desk partition: “Listen, asshole. If it was up to me, I’d throw the lot of you in a dumpster and set a match to it. So, stop pissing me off... or things are gonna get nasty.”

options.text: RESIGN THE MISSION: suggest he sort out his personal issues and let you work with someone more competent.
options.outcome: “I suggest you sort out your personal issues and let me work with someone more competent.” {{Hank}} grabs {{Connor}} by the collar and shoves him against the desk partition: “Listen, asshole. If it was up to me, I’d throw the lot of you in a dumpster and set a match to it. So, stop pissing me off... or things are gonna get nasty.”

options.text: THREATEN: say you will report to your superiors that he refuses to work on the investigation.
options.outcome: “I’m going to file a report with my superiors that you refuse to work on this investigation.” {{Hank}} grabs {{Connor}} by the collar and shoves him against the desk partition: “Listen, asshole. If it was up to me, I’d throw the lot of you in a dumpster and set a match to it. So, stop pissing me off... or things are gonna get nasty.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK IS MAD. Every answer costs a Hank small down (−1): the wiki (“When Hank gets angry with Connor (unavoidable)”), Relationship Stat (“When Hank gets mad at the end of Waiting for Hank”) and PowerPyx (“Connor can’t win with this one. All responses cause Hank▼”). This is the one arrow in the chapter the template does not show (it has no icon on these buttons or on the collar grab that follows); it is kept on the wiki’s authority and flagged for the operator. Then the collar grab, quoted from the template.

Officer {{Chris}} comes up to the desk: “Lieutenant... uh… sorry to disturb you. I have some information on the AX400 that killed the guy last night... It’s been sighted in the Ravendale district.”
