nodes.title: Morning in the parking lot
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is 10:25 in the morning, the day after you fled {{Todd}}’s house with {{Alice}}. You spent the night in an abandoned car in a fenced parking lot, and {{Alice}} is still asleep on the back seat. You get out quietly and leave her sleeping. Anyone who looks at you closely can still see an android: the LED on your temple, your hair as it was.

situationWhen.text: You are wearing the clothes you took from the laundromat.
You are still in your android uniform.

facts: You and {{Alice}} spent the night in an abandoned car in a parking lot; she is asleep, and you need to change how you look before you go anywhere.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} leaves {{Alice}} asleep in the car and looks around the lot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint MORNING IN PARKING LOT and the unmissable LEAVE ALICE ASLEEP IN CAR (PowerPyx: “simply exit the car”), one event. The start is chosen by Fugitives (where Kara slept); this row plays when she slept in the abandoned car (the module reads `ch10Shelter`, `shelter`, `karaRoute`, then `ch10Ending`, and falls back to the car). Date and time from the template (NOV 6TH, 2038, AM 10:25), without the year. The template has no Kara line before the wake-up; the description of what she still looks like is the chapter’s objective “Change appearance” (wiki infobox). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: The parking lot
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the fenced parking lot where you spent the night. {{Alice}} is asleep in the abandoned car. Before you wake her you can look around: old tires lie in front of the car, magazines on the ground beside them, a dumpster stands against the back wall, the car has a trunk, and the gate you came in by looks out on the street. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

situationWhen.text: Your hair is cut and the LED is gone.
The trunk is jammed shut.
Police are patrolling the street outside the gate.

options.text: FIND SOME RUSTED SCISSORS: pull the old scissors out of the tire in front of the car.
options.outcome: A pair of rusted scissors is stuck in a tire in front of the car. {{Kara}} pulls them out and kneels at the car’s side mirror.

options.text: FIND BURNT ANDROID: look behind the dumpster by the back wall.
options.fact: Behind a dumpster in the parking lot lies an android that was burned to death, an AX420 by the number on its uniform; above it someone has sprayed “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”.
options.outcome: Behind the dumpster lies an android that has been burned to death; the number on its uniform reads AX420. Sprayed on the wall above it: “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”.

options.text: READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”: the magazine lying in front of the car.
options.fact: {{Detroit}} Today, “Cyber-Wildlife”: {{CyberLife}} is about to open the first android zoo, in Los Angeles, showing animals that have become extinct in the last thirty years (turtles, polar bears, mountain gorillas, African elephants and several species of tiger), which it promises will be “more real than the real thing”. The cover adds that US life expectancy is now 91, and that 0.4% of the world’s population holds 94% of its wealth.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the magazine: {{CyberLife}} is opening an android zoo of extinct animals.

options.text: READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”: the other side of it.
options.fact: A travel advertisement for {{Canada}}: “where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.” Although the United States voted in its Android Act in 2028, the parliament there has again put off deciding whether to permit androids: they are not sold there and have no official status, while in the United States they fuel record growth and record unemployment.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the advertisement: across the border, androids are still not allowed.

options.text: TRY TO OPEN CAR TRUNK: see what is in the back of the car.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} tries the trunk. It is jammed and will not open; she needs something to force it.

options.text: FIND A CROWBAR: look for something to force the trunk with.
options.outcome: A crowbar lies on the other side of the car, near the fence that borders the abandoned house next door. {{Kara}} picks it up.

options.text: FIND SOME CLOTHES: force the trunk open with the crowbar and put on what is inside.
options.fact: You found clothes in the trunk of the abandoned car and changed out of your android uniform.
options.outcome: The trunk gives. Inside are some old clothes, a jacket among them. {{Kara}} takes off her android uniform and puts them on.

options.text: CHECK NEIGHBORHOOD: look out through the gate you came in by.
options.fact: Police are patrolling the street outside the parking lot; you need to reach the train station without being noticed.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks out through the gate. There are police in the street. {{Kara}}: “The police are on our trail… We need to reach the train station without being noticed.”

options.text: WAKE UP {{ALICE}}: go back to the car and wake her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}… Wake up, {{Alice}}…” {{Alice}}: “So it wasn’t a nightmare…” {{Kara}}: “No... No, it wasn’t a nightmare. How do you feel?” {{Alice}}: “I’m cold… What are we gonna do now?..” {{Kara}}: “That android we saw yesterday... he gave me an address, he said we could get help there. The train passes just on the other side of the road, the station can’t be far… You feel okay to walk a little? Let’s go then.” {{Alice}}: “You’re pretty like that. You really look like a human now.” They leave the parking lot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ EXPLORE PARKING LOT ] hub and the line out of it, as one repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet. Chart nodes, in the chart’s order: FIND SOME RUSTED SCISSORS (then the hair, next scene), FIND BURNT ANDROID, READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”, READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”, TRY TO OPEN CAR TRUNK > FIND A CROWBAR > FIND SOME CLOTHES (cross-chapter padlock; sets `clothes`), CHECK NEIGHBORHOOD with POLICE IS IN VICINITY (one option; PowerPyx: unmissable), then WAKE UP ALICE and LEAVE THE PARKING LOT (one option, with the template’s wake-up dialogue). The trunk needs Kara not to have taken the laundromat clothes in Fugitives (wiki: “only available if didn’t obtain clothes”). Leaving needs the haircut and the look at the street (the objective “Change appearance”; PowerPyx marks CHECK NEIGHBORHOOD unmissable). The two magazines are chart nodes inside the hub, so they are hub options here rather than a media scene; their facts are the wiki’s article text, without the interviewee’s name. The burnt android’s details are the wiki’s Notes (AX420, “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”). The car start has no Alice prompt and no stat arrow anywhere (template, wiki). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Cut and color your hair
nodes.whenNot: Kara never found the scissors.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, kneeling at the side mirror of the abandoned car with the rusted scissors. You are going to cut your hair short so that nobody looking for a runaway android will know you. What color will it be?

options.text: BROWN: cut it short and keep it brown.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and keeps it brown. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

options.text: BLACK: cut it short and dye it black.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and dyes it black. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

options.text: WHITE: cut it short and dye it white.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and dyes it white. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

options.text: BLONDE: cut it short and dye it blonde.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} cuts her hair short in the side mirror and dyes it blonde. Then she finds the LED on her temple with her fingers and tears it out.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CUT AND COLOR HAIR (cross-chapter padlock) with its group BROWN / BLACK / WHITE / BLONDE, in the chart’s order, and REMOVE LED (PowerPyx: “Unmissable, Kara will always rip it out after choosing her new haircut”), which is part of every outcome. In the car row it sits under FIND SOME RUSTED SCISSORS; the wiki’s Notes: she “will use one of the side mirrors of the abandoned car to cut her hair”. The template has no prompt for the hair (it is silent), so the labels are the chart’s and the string table’s (HAIRCOLOR choice group). The game also offers CHANGE / FINISH after a color (string table) to try another; only the final color is modelled. Recorded as `ch13Hair`; no later chapter is known to read it (research note §8 Q13). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: The supermarket
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with Lieutenant {{Hank}} outside the convenience store where the runaway AX400 was seen last night. {{Hank}} lets the bus driver go: “Alright, that’s all for now. Free to go.” Officer {{Ben}}: “We’ve got officers sweeping the neighborhood, in case anybody saw anything.” {{Hank}}: “Okay. Well, let me know if they turn anything up.” {{Ben}}: “What are you gonna do with that?” {{Hank}}: “I’ve no idea…” You: “It took the first bus that came along... and stayed at the end of the line. Its decision wasn’t planned, it was driven by fear.” {{Hank}}: “Androids don’t feel fear.” You: “Deviants do. They get overwhelmed by their emotions and make irrational decisions.” {{Hank}}: “Ah well, that still doesn’t tell us where it went.” You: “It didn’t have a plan, and it had nowhere to go. Maybe it didn’t go far...” {{Hank}}: “Maybe...”
facts: The AX400 took the first bus to the end of the line last night; the police are sweeping the neighborhood but have no lead.

outcomes.0: The police don’t have a lead.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint CONNOR INVESTIGATES SUPERMARKET and POLICE DON’T HAVE A LEAD (PowerPyx: “Unmissable, that’s just the way it is”), one event with the template’s dialogue for the parking-lot row. The wiki infobox has Connor playable here only if Kara is spotted, so it is narrated, not a decision. The template’s variant line for this row when Kara reaches the train unnoticed ({{Hank}}: “It won’t get far. We’ll find it sooner or later. Let’s go.”) is not built: it belongs to a Connor scene after the sneak that the chart does not show. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Morning in the motel
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in room 28 of the motel where you spent the night with {{Alice}}. It is 10:25 in the morning, the day after you fled {{Todd}}’s house. You are wearing the clothes you took from the laundromat; the LED is still on your temple. {{Alice}} wakes up. You: “I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to wake you…” {{Alice}}: “So, it wasn’t a nightmare…” You: “No... No, it wasn’t a nightmare…”
facts: You and {{Alice}} spent the night in room 28 of a motel; it is the morning after you fled {{Todd}}’s house.

outcomes.0: {{Alice}} is awake.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint MORNING IN MOTEL, with the template’s first lines. Plays when Kara slept in the motel in Fugitives (which needs the laundromat clothes, so she is dressed). Room 28 is the receptionist’s line later in the chapter. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Talk to {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, beside {{Alice}} in the motel room. She has just woken up and remembered last night. What do you say to her?

options.text: BATH?: offer her a nice warm bath, and then food.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “How about a nice, warm bath? And then we can go out and try to get you something to eat. What do you say?” {{Alice}} nods. {{Kara}}: “Okay. I’ll run you a bath.”

options.text: HUNGRY?: say she must be starving; a bath, then you will find her something to eat.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You must be starving… You should take a bath, and then we’ll go out and find you something to eat. What do you say?” {{Alice}} nods. {{Kara}}: “Okay. I’ll run you a bath.”

options.text: TIRED?: tell her it is still early and she should sleep some more.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s still early. You should try to get some more sleep.” {{Alice}}: “I’m not tired anymore.” {{Kara}}: “Okay. I’ll run you a bath.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO ALICE: the template’s prompt BATH? / HUNGRY? / TIRED?, in its order. Alice small up on BATH? and on HUNGRY? (template arrows; wiki: “Choosing either “bath?” or “hungry?” after waking up in the motel”), +1 each; TIRED? has no arrow. The string table also has a fourth button, FEEL? (“How do you feel? You were really exhausted last night.” / “I’m okay.”), which the template does not place; it is not built. Alice’s nod is inferred (the template goes straight to “Okay. I’ll run you a bath.”).

nodes.title: The motel room
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the motel room with {{Alice}}. You have said you will run her a bath; the bathroom is through the door. In the room there is a clock, a window onto the street, a painting on the wall, and the television, with magazines in front of it. You still need to change how you look: your hair, and the LED on your temple. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

situationWhen.text: The bath is running.
Your hair is cut and the LED is gone; the bath is still filling.

options.text: DRAW A BATH FOR {{ALICE}}: go into the bathroom and start the water.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns on the bath taps. While the tub fills she looks at her face in the mirror over the sink: the face of the runaway AX400.

options.text: LOOK AT THE CLOCK.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks at the clock. The morning is getting on.

options.text: LOOK OUTSIDE: look out of the window at the street.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks out of the window at the street outside the motel.

options.text: READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”: the magazine in front of the television.
options.fact: {{Detroit}} Today, “Cyber-Wildlife”: {{CyberLife}} is about to open the first android zoo, in Los Angeles, showing animals that have become extinct in the last thirty years (turtles, polar bears, mountain gorillas, African elephants and several species of tiger), which it promises will be “more real than the real thing”. The cover adds that US life expectancy is now 91, and that 0.4% of the world’s population holds 94% of its wealth.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the magazine: {{CyberLife}} is opening an android zoo of extinct animals.

options.text: READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”: the other side of it.
options.fact: A travel advertisement for {{Canada}}: “where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.” Although the United States voted in its Android Act in 2028, the parliament there has again put off deciding whether to permit androids: they are not sold there and have no official status, while in the United States they fuel record growth and record unemployment.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the advertisement: across the border, androids are still not allowed.

options.text: LOOK AT THE PAINTING on the wall.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks at the painting on the motel room wall.

options.text: FINISH DRAWING BATH: turn off the taps; the bath is ready.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns off the water and comes back into the room. {{Alice}} looks at her: “You’re pretty like that. You really look like a human now.” {{Kara}}: “Your bath’s ready.”

options.text: CHANGE CHANNEL: watch the news with {{Alice}} without running the bath.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays in the room with {{Alice}} and turns to the television.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DRAW A BATH FOR ALICE (then the hair, next scene), [ EXPLORE MOTEL ROOM ] with LOOK AT THE CLOCK, LOOK OUTSIDE, READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”, READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}” and LOOK AT THE PAINTING, and FINISH DRAWING BATH, as one repeatable scene. The chart lets Kara explore before the bath (TALK TO ALICE has an edge straight to the hub) or after REMOVE LED, and FINISH DRAWING BATH bypasses the hub, so here the room can be explored any time before the bath is finished, which ends the phase and needs the haircut (Alice’s compliment follows it in the template). The sources give nothing about the clock, the window or the painting, so their outcomes say only what Kara looks at. The magazines are chart nodes inside the hub; their facts are the wiki’s article text. Outcome lines are the template’s (“You’re pretty like that…”, “Your bath’s ready.”). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one. The direct TALK TO ALICE > EXPLORE MOTEL ROOM > CHANGE CHANNEL edge is also available without starting the bath or haircut. This follows the chart; whether the game forces a haircut elsewhere on that edge remains an operator check (research §8.5).

nodes.title: The news
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the motel room with {{Alice}}. You change the channel on the television to the news.

situationWhen.text: A reporter, {{JossDouglas}} for {{Channel16}}: “The victim’s name was {{Todd}} {{Williams}}, an unemployed man from {{Corktown}}. According to initial reports, he was shot by his android, an AX400. The android fled the scene and a police search is now in progress. Reporting live for {{Channel16}} News, I’m {{JossDouglas}}.”
{{Alice}}: “You had no choice… He would have killed me if you hadn’t stopped him…”
{{Alice}}: “I didn’t wanna hurt him, but he was gonna kill us…”

A reporter, {{JossDouglas}} for {{Channel16}}: “Thanks, {{Michael}}. I’m joined by {{Corktown}} resident {{Todd}} {{Williams}}, who was violently attacked by his AX400 around 11 PM last night. {{Todd}}, can you tell us what happened?” {{Todd}}: “I was having dinner, I was minding my own business. Damn thing jumped on me. Managed to defend myself, but it went crazy. I thought it was gonna kill me... So I fought it off, but it ran away.” {{JossDouglas}}: “Thank you, {{Todd}}. Disturbing news for android owners everywhere. Police have launched a search to find the android. Let’s hope they find it fast.” {{Alice}}: “It’s not true… He’s lying… He’s the one who tried to hurt us…”

facts: The morning news is reporting on what happened at {{Todd}}’s house, and the police are searching for the android.

outcomes.0: {{Alice}} has heard all of it.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CHANGE CHANNEL and ALICE HEARS ABOUT TODD, one event: the chart shows no edge around CHANGE CHANNEL, and the conversation that follows needs it, so it is not optional (research note §8 Q4). The broadcast and Alice’s reaction are the template’s three variants: Todd killed and Kara shot him, Todd killed and Alice shot him, Todd alive. Neither report mentions Alice (Alice page). Public opinion small down on both variants (template arrows; wiki On_the_Run: “Todd was killed or injured … Kara switches on the TV”), −1. This replaces the old media scene R13, whose murder report wrongly searched for “the android and a child”. Who shot Todd is read from Stormy Night (`ch07Ending` or `toddShooter` matching Alice; otherwise Kara).

nodes.title: “What are we gonna do?”
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the motel room. {{Alice}}: “What are we gonna do? We have nowhere to go… And the police are looking for us now.”

options.text: CAN’T STAY HERE: tell her you cannot stay; you have no money.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We can’t stay here, we don’t have any money…”

options.text: FAMILY: ask whether she has any family who could help.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Do you have any family? Anyone who could help us?” {{Alice}}: “No… there was just dad.”

options.text: CONTACT ANDROID: suggest the address the android gave you yesterday.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “That android yesterday… he gave me an address… He said we could get help there… Could be worth a try.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Not a chart node: the template’s live prompt CAN’T STAY HERE / FAMILY / CONTACT ANDROID after the report, in its order, with Alice’s line before it. The template’s other prompt here (REASSURING / ANALYTICAL / VULNERABLE / SINCERE) is cut content and is not built. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Cheer {{Alice}} up
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}} in the motel room. She is frightened, and she has nobody but you. You kneel beside her. What do you tell her?

options.text: MOVING: tell her that something ties you together and nothing will ever separate you.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I know I’m just a… a machine… But, I feel as if something ties us together… I want you to know, no matter what happens... nothing will ever separate us.”

options.text: DETERMINED: tell her you are going to pull through as long as you are together.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We’re going to pull through this, {{Alice}}. As long as we’re together, nothing can hurt us.”

options.text: COMFORTING: tell her you cannot change the past, but you can decide the future.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We can’t change the past, {{Alice}}... But we can decide the future... We’re gonna pull through, and soon all this will just be a bad memory.”

options.text: SUPPORTIVE: tell her it is the two of you against the world, and you will make her happy again.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s us against the world, {{Alice}}… Just the two of us… We have to learn to trust each other… I only have you, and you only have me… And I’m going to do everything I can to make you happy again.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CHEER ALICE UP (dialogue node): the template’s prompt MOVING / DETERMINED / COMFORTING / SUPPORTIVE, in its order. Alice small up on each (template arrows; wiki: “any of the 4 options”), +1. The kneeling is the string table’s KNEEL beat.

nodes.title: Breakfast
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You: “Finish getting ready. I’ll go out and find some food for you, then we can get going.” You step out of the room to look for breakfast. Police cars are pulling up at the motel office.
facts: The police arrived at the motel while you were out looking for breakfast.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} hurries back for {{Alice}}. They have to get out before the police reach the room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s LOOK FOR BREAKFAST and KARA SPOTS POLICE FORCES, one event, with the template’s line. That Kara goes back for Alice is inferred: the chart continues with Connor at the desk, and Hank finds the room empty. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: The motel desk
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The trail of the runaway AX400 has led you and Lieutenant {{Hank}} to a motel. At the desk, {{Hank}}: “Lieutenant {{Anderson}}, {{Detroit}} Police. We’re looking for a female android, robbed a store down the road last night. You see anything?” The receptionist: “An android? No… I don’t take androids here.” You hold up her picture: “Have you seen anyone that looks like this?” The receptionist: “Fuck… I knew there was something weird about her… She came in last night – she was dressed normal, you know... There was no way I could tell.” {{Hank}}: “Is it still here?” The receptionist: “Yeah, probably. Room 28.” {{Hank}}: “Thank you.”
facts: The motel receptionist said the AX400 checked in last night dressed as a human and is probably still in room 28.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}}, on the radio: “{{Ben}}?.. Yeah, it’s still at the motel. Send some uniforms and cordon off the area. I’m heading to its room now.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint CONNOR INVESTIGATES THE MOTEL and INTERROGATE RECEPTIONIST, one event: the template has no prompt at the desk, only the dialogue (“Police is at the motel”). The receptionist is not named. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: “You wait in the car.”
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, outside the motel office. {{Hank}} has called for backup and is heading to room 28. He turns to you: “You wait in the car.”

options.text: RATIONAL: tell him he will need you; you know more about androids than he does.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’re going to need me, Lieutenant. I know more about androids than you do.” {{Hank}}: “Listen, I’m tired of you talkin’ back to me. You’re a machine, so shut the fuck up and do what I say!” {{Connor}}: “All I want is to accomplish my mission. I’m sorry if that upsets you.” {{Hank}}: “Wanna see the end of your mission? Stop busting my fucking balls…”

options.text: DIPLOMATIC: say you think it is best if you go with him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I think it’s best if I go with you.” {{Hank}}: “Listen, I’m tired of you talkin’ back to me. You’re a machine, so shut the fuck up and do what I say!” {{Connor}}: “All I want is to accomplish my mission. I’m sorry if that upsets you.” {{Hank}}: “Wanna see the end of your mission? Stop busting my fucking balls…”

options.text: DIRECT: refuse; you are coming with him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Out of the question. I’m coming with you.” {{Hank}}: “Listen, I’m tired of you talkin’ back to me. You’re a machine, so shut the fuck up and do what I say!” {{Connor}}: “All I want is to accomplish my mission. I’m sorry if that upsets you.” {{Hank}}: “Wanna see the end of your mission? Stop busting my fucking balls…”

nodes.adaptationNote: Not a chart node: the template’s prompt RATIONAL / DIPLOMATIC / DIRECT, in its order; every answer gets the same reply. Hank small down on every option, −1, from the wiki only (On_the_Run: “any of the three dialogue choices … outside the hotel desk (unavoidable)”; Relationship_Stat: “Any response to Hank asking Connor to wait in the car”). The template has no arrow here, as it has none for Connor anywhere in the chapter; the wiki states it on two pages, so it is applied and flagged for the operator to confirm in game.

nodes.title: Room 28
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You follow {{Hank}} toward the stairs up to room 28. To the right of the stairs, in the corner, there is a blue door.

options.text: FOLLOW {{HANK}}: go up to room 28 with him.
options.outcome: {{Hank}} opens room 28. It is empty. {{Hank}}: “It’s gone…”

options.text: CHECK THE DOOR: open the blue door in the corner.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} opens the blue door. The AX400 and the girl are on the other side, slipping away. {{Connor}}: “Found you.” They run, and {{Connor}} goes after them.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FOLLOW HANK, then HANK CHECKS MOTEL ROOM (to KARA & ALICE IN THE STREET) or CHECK THE DOOR (straight to CONNOR PURSUES KARA). HANK CHECKS MOTEL ROOM (“It’s gone…”, template) is the first option’s outcome; “Found you.” is the string table’s BACKDOOR line. CHECK THE DOOR sets `chase`. nodes.title: In the street
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out on the street with {{Alice}}. The train station is a few blocks down the road. Between you and it, police officers are posted along both sides of the street. To get there unseen you would have to move from cover to cover, crossing from one side to the other when nobody is looking.

situationWhen.text: You got out of the motel before the police reached room 28.

facts: Police are watching the street between you and the train station.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}}’s hand and walks toward the train station.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint KARA & ALICE IN THE STREET and WALK TOWARD TRAIN STATION, one event. Reached from the parking lot, and from the motel after FOLLOW HANK. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Getting past the police
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, holding {{Alice}}’s hand on a street full of police. The station is ahead. Officers stand on both sides of the street; there is a bus shelter by the laundromat, umbrellas outside a café, an ATM, and gaps in the traffic to cross in.

options.text: SNEAK PAST POLICE FORCES: go from cover to cover, crossing whenever the officers look away.
options.outcome: Across to the motel side, behind the bus shelter by the laundromat, a fast dash over the road, under an umbrella, behind the ATM: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} slip past every officer.

options.text: Walk straight down the street to the station without hiding.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} walk down the street in the open.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group SNEAK PAST POLICE FORCES / SPOTTED BY POLICE. In the game it is a stealth sequence, not a menu; the string table lists its steps (avoid the cops in front of the squat and the motel, cross to the coffee shop, hide near the laundromat, cross to the bank, hide using an umbrella, hide in the pawn shop), and PowerPyx gives the route (motel side, bus shelter, “cross the street fast. If you are a bit too slow, you will be spotted”, umbrella, ATM). Sneaking is one action with a failure branch; walking in the open always gets them SPOTTED BY POLICE. The risk value is unsourced: no source gives a probability for any check in this chapter (research note §3); Experienced difficulty is modelled, so every chart failure branch is reachable. Fixes the old K09: walking openly now always leads to the chase and never to a death in the street (the chart has no death before CONNOR PURSUES KARA), and the old situation’s “the news is calling you a kidnapper” is gone (no report mentions Alice). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Upstairs

nodes.title: Interrogate the squat android
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the squat, facing the scarred android. What do you ask him?

options.text: AX400: ask whether he has seen an AX400.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m looking for an AX400. Have you seen it?” The android: “{{Ralph}}’s seen nobody…”

options.text: DEVIANTS: ask whether there are any other androids here.

nodes.title: The red mural
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the platform. A man walks past on his phone: “Hey. Yeah, I’m good. How about you? … I know! It’s crazy, right? Sure, I’ll talk to you later.” A homeless man stops you: “Hey, mister, can you spare some change?..” Two passengers are talking: “I heard that android boyband is going to win some music prize.” “God, they are so creepy.” “My kids don’t listen to anything else.” To your left as you came off the train, a large red mural covers the wall: a figure with a halo and, on its chest inside a red circle, a small mark, a square with an arrowhead above and below it and a bar on either side. Nobody else on the platform looks at it twice. You scan the mark, and the key in your memory decodes it: it is a sign left for androids, and it shows you what the next sign looks like.

nodes.title: A magazine on the bench
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the platform at {{Ferndale}} Station, before the escalators down to the street. Someone has left a digital magazine on a bench; you can swipe from one cover story to the next.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Android on the Run!
facts: Residents of a {{Detroit}} suburb watched a chase after a police manhunt, with roadblocks and dozens of police interviews, flushed out a fugitive. The rogue AX400 model is thought to be suffering from an extremely rare malfunction and took extreme measures to avoid the police, even dashing across a busy highway. Eyewitness statements are inconclusive, there is no official report, and no {{CyberLife}} spokesperson was available for comment.

media.title: Tech Addict: {{CyberLife}}’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer
facts: {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a quantum supercomputer capable of “exaflops”, a billion billion operations per second. It will calculate the probability of mass-extinction events, such as aggressive alien invasions or global disasters like meteors or superviruses, so that humanity can anticipate and prepare for them.

media.title: Tech Addict: Android Astronauts to Explore Io
facts: NASA has launched a crew of five androids on a three-year journey to Io, one of Jupiter’s moons: the first all-machine crew. NASA’s director calls androids an extraordinary asset for the conquest of space, because cosmic radiation destroys human DNA. No return journey is planned; the androids will work on Io for several months before the extreme conditions destroy them.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s three magazine nodes, READ “ON THE RUN”, READ “FORTUNE TELLER” and READ “ANDROID ASTRONAUTS”: covers of one magazine on a bench on the platform (wiki: “on a bench right after Markus gets off the train”; PowerPyx: “before going down the escalator”, “Swipe right to change cover topics”). Android Astronauts to Explore Io (Tech Addict #13) is always there. Android on the Run! (Detroit Today #32) appears only if Kara and Alice were pursued by Connor in On the Run (wiki); CyberLife’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer (Tech Addict #15) appears otherwise. The pursuit is read from On the Run’s flag (`chase`), set whenever the highway chase began, including when it ended with Kara and Alice dead on the highway; a PowerPyx reader’s unconfirmed list puts that case and KARA & ALICE VANISHED under Fortune Teller, but the wiki’s condition is the pursuit itself. Article facts are condensed from the wiki’s magazine pages; NASA’s director, CyberLife’s Director of Futurology and the suburb (Camden) are left unnamed. Corrected from the earlier version of this scene: the article mentions no child, the “extremely rare malfunction” is not a CyberLife statement (no spokesperson was available), and the chapter is in daylight (04:30 PM), not at night. No public-opinion effect: no source gives one.

Asking does not replace the trail: whichever option is taken, the next scene follows the signs. {{Markus}}’s question is the template’s line; the template has no reply, so the android gives none (PowerPyx: “At the bottom of the escalator, talk to the android on the left side waiting at the bus stop”; the game’s key calls it the parked android). The man bumping into {{Markus}} and the mother and child are the template’s. The two people talking about {{Carl}} are the template’s condition group (Carl died in Broken, or Carl is alive), chosen from `carl`; what they say is added to what {{Markus}} knows. {{Carl}}’s surname is a name token. No risk and no stat change.

nodes.title: Following the signs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, following the trail through the streets. The lion-and-boxer mural holds two marks; you scan both, and the preview leads you on. Across the street, past two crosswalks, a building wall is painted with a colorful rainbow, and two more marks are hidden in it. A homeless man calls to the passers-by: “I need a dollar, I haven’t eaten all day! … Spare some change?” Children are playing nearby: “Tag! You’re it!” “I’m gonna catch you!” You keep to the left sidewalk down to where the street ends at a fence. Behind it, on a wall, is a mural of a robot. Through the fence you can scan two of its marks; the third is hidden behind a wooden plank leaning against the wall.
facts: The marks led you from mural to mural down the street, to a fenced-off wall where the street ends.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} reaches the fence at the end of the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: FOLLOW THE SIGNS: graffiti #2 (lion and boxer, after the escalators, 2 marks), #3 (rainbow, across the street, 2 marks) and the two visible marks of #4 (robot, behind the fence), from PowerPyx’s graffiti guide and its screenshot counters. The homeless man and the children are the template’s ambient lines, abridged. No choice, no risk and no stat change: the chapter’s template has no prompt, clue or arrow, and the wiki lists no probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it.

nodes.title: The junkyard
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Once you have scanned the two marks you can see, you crouch and crawl under the fence, stand, and move the wooden plank away from the wall. The robot mural’s third mark was behind it; you scan it. The streets are behind you now: you come out into a junkyard of wrecked cars and scrap. On the wall to the left is a large white mural of a head, the next sign. To the left of where you came in, a white car blocks your view of the corner behind it.

options.text: Look behind the white car to the left of where you came in.
options.fact: Hidden behind a white car in a junkyard on the trail lay a dead android.
options.outcome: Behind the white car lies a dead android, hidden where it fell. {{Markus}} looks at it, then goes back to the trail.

options.text: Go straight to the white mural.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} crosses the junkyard to the white mural.

nodes.adaptationNote: LEAVE THE STREETS (PowerPyx: the crawl prompt appears once the two visible marks are scanned; “remove the wooden plank leaning against the wall that blocks the 4th Graffiti”; the game’s Crouch, Remove and Stand prompts) and the optional SEE ANDROID BODY beside it (PowerPyx: “Check on the left side from where you entered. There’s a dead android hidden behind a white car, easy to miss this one”; wiki: “to the left when entering the parking lot”). The body is an option; either way the next scene goes on with CONTINUE ON THE JERICHO TRAIL. No source describes the body further or gives it an effect. Casual mode’s “Obstrued symbol” hint is not modelled (the benchmark plays Experienced). No risk and no stat change.

nodes.title: The dumpster
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the white mural of a head. From the ground you can scan only one of its marks; the others are out of sight from here. A dumpster stands nearby. You pull it over to the wall beside the mural, climb onto it and pull yourself up onto the roof.
facts: Some of the trail’s marks can only be seen from above; it took you up onto the rooftops.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} is up on the roof.

nodes.adaptationNote: CONTINUE ON THE JERICHO TRAIL and USE THE DUMPSTER TO CLIMB UP, linear and unmissable (PowerPyx: “After scanning the first clue on the 5th Graffiti in the Junkyard (the white-colored one that looks like a person’s head), you will have to pull a dumpster to a wall to climb up.”). No choice, no risk and no stat change: the chapter’s template has no prompt, clue or arrow, and the wiki lists no probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it.

nodes.title: Across the gap
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the roof. From up here you can see the white mural’s other two marks: a black one on the far left of the head, and a white one on its forehead just above the eye, almost invisible against the white paint. You scan both. Across the roof, the building ends at a gap over a drop, and the trail goes on beyond it. You preconstruct the way across, running each move in your mind before you make it, then take it: a run, a kick off the wall, and you land on the far side and drop down into the next yard.
facts: You crossed a gap between rooftops by preconstructing the route first, rehearsing each move in your mind.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} lands in the next yard.

nodes.adaptationNote: REACH THE ROOF (checkpoint) and CROSS THE GAP. The rooftop marks of graffiti #5 are PowerPyx’s (“a white shape just above the head’s eye, on the forehead”; “a black “X” shape on the far left side of the head”). PowerPyx: “Preconstruct the path to take. Do a wall jump to cross over to the other side.” The wall jump is scripted traversal: no source describes {{Markus}} falling or failing, the chart has no failure node, and {{Markus}} cannot die before Freedom March (Markus page), so it carries no risk. Preconstruction is {{Markus}}’s ability to preview a route (RK200 page). The chart’s optional SEE ANDROID BODY drawn beside REACH THE ROOF is found after the jump (PowerPyx: “Drop down into the next yard”; the wiki lists it under Cross the Gap), so it is offered in the next scene. No stat change.

nodes.title: The yard
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in a yard of containers below a tall brick building. High on its wall is a faded red advertisement for spark plugs, and the preview tells you the next sign is in it. A climbing route leads up the building toward a door. The far left side of the yard, by a container, is still unexplored.

options.text: Look around the far left side of the yard, by the container.
options.fact: Another dead android lay next to a container in a yard further along the trail.
options.outcome: Next to a container on the far side of the yard lies another dead android. {{Markus}} leaves it there and turns back to the building.

options.text: Go straight to the building.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} turns to the building.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional SEE ANDROID BODY beside REACH THE ROOF and CROSS THE GAP (wiki: “next to a container”; PowerPyx: “There’s another android body here, relatively easy to see on the far left side of the area (in area with 6th Graffiti). Just be sure to look at it before climbing up to the next building.”). The advertisement is described from PowerPyx’s screenshot of graffiti #6. Either way the next scene goes on with REACH THE DOOR. No effect is sourced. No risk and no stat change.

nodes.title: The abandoned office
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, below the tall building. You scan the three marks in the faded advertisement. Then you preconstruct a way up: keep to the left wall, jump for the ladder, pull yourself up. You climb it the way you saw it, reach the door at the top and go in. Inside is an abandoned office, dim and empty, with pillars across the room and a broken wall at one side.
facts: The trail led up a building wall and into an abandoned office.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} is inside the abandoned office.

nodes.adaptationNote: Graffiti #6 (3 marks; PowerPyx: “looks like an advertisement on the tall building overlooking the yard”), REACH THE DOOR (PowerPyx: “you can Preconstruct another climbing path that leads up to the building. Stick to the left wall and jump on the ladder to pull yourself up.”) and EXPLORE ABANDONED OFFICE (“Completes automatically when you’ve climbed into the building”). The climb has no failure branch and carries no risk. No choice, no risk and no stat change: the chapter’s template has no prompt, clue or arrow, and the wiki lists no probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it.

nodes.title: The office
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the abandoned office. The preview of the last sign matches no single surface: part of it is painted on a pillar and part on the wall behind, and it will only come together from the right spot. Straight ahead of the door, a pillar hides part of the room from view.

options.text: Look behind the pillar straight ahead.
options.fact: A third dead android sat propped against a pillar in an abandoned office on the trail.
options.outcome: Propped up against the pillar sits a dead android. {{Markus}} looks at it for a moment before going back to the sign.

options.text: Look for the spot where the last sign comes together.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} starts walking the room, looking for the angle.

nodes.adaptationNote: The optional SEE ANDROID BODY in the office (PowerPyx: “When you enter the room it’s straight ahead, hidden behind a pillar”; wiki: “propped up against a pillar”). Either way the next scene is FIND THE RIGHT EXIT. No effect is sourced. No risk and no stat change.

nodes.title: The ship
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, moving around the office until a pillar lines up with the wall behind it and the two halves of the last mark become one. You scan it. It points you to the rubble behind the broken wall at the side of the room. You climb through and come out into the open, above the old docks. Below lies a huge, rusted freighter, its blue hull lettered in big white capitals: {{JERICHO}}.
facts: {{Jericho}} is an old rusted freighter at the abandoned docks, its name painted on the hull. The trail of marks ends there.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has found {{Jericho}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: FIND THE RIGHT EXIT (PowerPyx: “Scan the 7th and final Graffiti by lining up a pillar with part of the wall … interact with the rubble behind the broken wall on the side of the room. It leads outside to the next area.”) and LOCATE JERICHO (checkpoint; PowerPyx: “You see a short cutscene when you go outside”; the chart’s picture tile shows the rusted blue hull lettered JERICHO; the wiki calls the ship an abandoned freighter). The lining-up is a puzzle that cannot fail. No choice, no risk and no stat change: the chapter’s template has no prompt, clue or arrow, and the wiki lists no probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it.

nodes.title: The docks
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the docks by the ship. Straight ahead, an old rusted bridge leads out toward it. At the end of the area, past a metal railing and a stairway, a crane stands over the ship with its arm reaching out above the hull.

options.text: Walk out onto the bridge straight ahead.
options.fact: A rusted bridge on the docks collapsed when you tried to cross it toward the ship.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} walks out along the bridge. Before he can cross, the rusted bridge collapses. He is not hurt; he goes back the way he came and heads for the crane.

options.text: Head for the crane at the end of the area.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} heads for the crane.

nodes.adaptationNote: LOCATE JERICHO has two lines out: the optional detour WALK BRIDGE → BRIDGE COLLAPSES, which rejoins the main line at CLIMB CRANE AND JUMP, and a line straight to the crane. PowerPyx: “walk on the bridge straight ahead of you”; “When you walk the bridge for long enough it collapses. No worries, it won’t kill you. Backtrack to where you came from.” The collapse is scripted, not a failure, so it has no risk; how far {{Markus}} gets before it goes is not described. Either way the next scene is the crane. No stat change.

nodes.title: The crane
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You climb the metal railing at the end of the area, go up the stairs and climb the ladder onto the crane. You walk out along its arm to the very end, high above the ship, with dark water below. You jump.
facts: To get into {{Jericho}} you jumped from the arm of a crane into the water inside the ship.

outcomes.0: Everything goes black for a moment.

nodes.adaptationNote: CLIMB CRANE AND JUMP (PowerPyx: “climb up a metallic railing at the end of the area. Then go upstairs and climb the ladder. Once on top walk to the end of the crane and jump down into the water. The screen fades to black for a moment.”). A deliberate, scripted jump that always lands safely (“You will have landed safely in water inside the Jericho ship”), so it carries no risk. Readers say {{Markus}} loses his coat in the water; not modelled. No choice, no risk and no stat change: the chapter’s template has no prompt, clue or arrow, and the wiki lists no probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it.

nodes.title: Inside the boat
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, surfacing in water inside the ship. It is almost completely dark. You pull yourself up a ladder to a heavy door and work its handle slowly until it opens. In a metal case on the wall beyond, you find a flashlight and take it. Its beam shows a long corridor lined with yellow hatches; the ones that open lead only to empty rooms, and the rest are locked. At the end of the corridor you get under some rubble and open the yellow hatch on the left. It leads into the machine room.
facts: Inside, {{Jericho}} is dark and flooded: corridors of locked hatches and empty rooms.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} steps into the machine room.

nodes.adaptationNote: INSIDE THE BOAT (checkpoint), FIND A FLASHLIGHT and ENTER THE MACHINE ROOM, linear (PowerPyx: the ladder; the door that on Experienced is opened by turning the controller “very very slowly”; “you must pick up a flashlight, it’s in a metallic case on a wall”; yellow hatches that “are either locked or just have empty rooms behind them”; the one that matters is “at the end of the corridor after going under some rubble … on the left”; the game’s prompt “Take Flashlight”). The door control is an input hurdle with no failure branch, so no risk. The three side rooms the wiki lists as unused are not included. No choice, no risk and no stat change: the chapter’s template has no prompt, clue or arrow, and the wiki lists no probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it.

nodes.title: The people of {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the machine room. You go down the metal stairs and out across a catwalk. It collapses under you and you fall. When you look up, you are not alone: androids stand around you in the dark, staring at you. One of them steps forward. “Welcome to {{Jericho}}.”
facts: You found {{Jericho}}. Other androids are hiding in the dark inside the ship, and one of them welcomed you.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has met the people of {{Jericho}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: FALL OFF CATWALK (PowerPyx: “Simply continue down the metallic stairs and across the catwalk. It will collapse and Markus falls down.”) and the chapter’s one ending, MET PEOPLE OF JERICHO (PowerPyx: “After Markus falls down he sees other androids staring at him. This is the only outcome to this linear level.”; template: Simon’s “Welcome to Jericho.”, the chapter’s last line). The ending is recorded in state as `ch14Ending`. The androids stay unnamed here: the introductions (“Who are you?”) open the next {{Markus}} chapter in the template (Time to Decide, In Jericho). No stat change: the first changes in how {{Jericho}}, {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} regard {{Markus}} come in Time to Decide.

nodes.title: Lunch break
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is November 6th, 2038, early afternoon. You get out of the car and follow Lieutenant {{Hank}} to a food truck on a street corner, where he eats most days. {{Hank}}: “Whoa! Hey! Hey! Hey!” The owner, {{Gary}}: “{{Hank}}. How’ you doing?” {{Hank}}: “Eh, you know, same old shit.” {{Gary}}, looking at you: “Plastic with you?” {{Hank}}: “Only temporary…” A man at the serving hatch, {{Pedro}}: “Hey, hey, hey... {{Hank}}! How you doin’, man?” {{Hank}}: “¡Ese!” {{Pedro}}: “Hey, listen, I got a shit-hot tip for you. Number five in the third, Lickety-split! That filly’s one hell of a chaser. You wanna flutter?” {{Hank}}: “Last shit-hot tip you gave me set me back a week’s wages, {{Pedro}}…” {{Pedro}}: “Come on, this is different, it’s 100% guaranteed. You can’t go wrong.” {{Hank}}: “Yeah, right… Alright, I’m in.” {{Pedro}}: “Damn straight! Hey! You won’t regret this!” Your objective reads RECONCILE WITH LT. {{HANK}}.
facts: At the food truck where {{Hank}} eats, {{Pedro}} sold him a tip on a horse race (number five in the third) and {{Hank}} took the bet, although the last tip cost him a week’s wages.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} stands at the serving hatch beside {{Hank}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint LUNCH BREAK and the node JOIN HANK, played only when {{Connor}} did not die in On the Run (the template’s variant “Hank and Connor arrive together”, lock “Connor didn’t die in On The Run”). Every line is the template’s. The objective is the game’s HUD string THOUGHTS.0501C.RECONCILIATE, with the token standing in for the surname. Watching {{Hank}} with {{Pedro}} here is what the template calls “Watch Hank with Pedro”, the lock on [GAMBLING]; a PowerPyx commenter confirms that being near the conversation is enough, so it is unlocked on every path that plays this scene. The gambler’s and the owner’s names are neutral tokens. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} insults {{Connor}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}: the replacement sent after the body that was hit by a truck on the freeway this morning, carrying its memory. You find Lieutenant {{Hank}} at the food truck where he eats lunch. The owner, {{Gary}}, hands him his food: “Here you go.” “Yeah, thanks.” “{{Hank}}. How’ you doing?” “Uh, you know, same old shit.” “Usual.” “Yeah.” Then {{Hank}} sees you: “What the fuck?..” You: “Sorry, Lieutenant. It took me a while to find you.” {{Hank}}: “Are you gonna come back like this every time you get killed?” You: “My predecessor was unfortunately destroyed, but {{CyberLife}} transferred its memory and sent me to replace it. This incident should not affect the investigation.” {{Hank}}: “Not affect the investigation? I just saw you get... hit by a truck! Now you come back like if nothing happened!” You: “A machine was destroyed. And another machine was sent to replace it. I don’t understand what’s bothering you.” {{Hank}}: “Okay, fuck you. Fuck you!”
facts: {{Hank}} saw your predecessor hit by a truck on the freeway, and was furious that you came back as if nothing had happened: “Are you gonna come back like this every time you get killed?”

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} turns back to his food. There is no lunch conversation.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK INSULTS CONNOR, the template’s variant “Connor finds Hank” (death unlock “Connor died in On The Run”), which replaces the whole conversation at the food truck (PowerPyx: “it will skip all the other dialogues in this section”). Every line is the template’s. Hank relationship small down (the template’s app-relation on this variant; wiki: “Connor died in On the Run”, down icon), applied here as −1. The engine still applies the pre-rebuild default death effect when {{Connor}} dies in On the Run (which includes Hank −1 at that moment); once chapter 13 is rebuilt without that Hank arrow, this is the only Hank change for the death, as the wiki has it. Read defensively: the scene plays if chapter 13 sets `ch13ConnorDied`, or, until it does, if the On the Run highway choice C09 was the pursuit and its roll failed.

nodes.title: The food truck
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the food truck while {{Hank}} waits for his order. Your scan can analyze the people and things around you, one at a time; when you are done, step up to {{Hank}}.

options.text: Scan {{Pedro}}, the man who sold {{Hank}} the tip.
options.fact: Your scan of {{Pedro}}: {{AABDAR}}, {{PEDRO}}; born 01/25/2005, unemployed; criminal record: illegal gambling, fraud.
options.outcome: {{AABDAR}}, {{PEDRO}} | Born: 01/25/2005 // Unemployed | Criminal record: Illegal gambling, fraud

options.text: Scan {{Hank}}.
options.fact: Your scan of {{Hank}}: born 09/06/1985, police lieutenant; criminal record: none.
options.outcome: LT. {{ANDERSON}}, {{HANK}} | Born: 09/06/1985 // Police Lieutenant | Criminal Record: None

options.text: Scan {{Gary}}, the owner, inside the truck.
options.fact: Your scan of {{Gary}}: {{KAYES}}, {{GARY}}; born 12/03/1988, business owner; criminal record: resisting arrest, breach of hygiene regulations.
options.outcome: {{KAYES}}, {{GARY}} | Born: 12/03/1988 // Business owner | Criminal record: Resisting arrest, breach of hygiene regulations

options.text: Scan the food hygiene license at the upper left of the serving hatch.
options.fact: The food truck’s hygiene license expired on 05/20/2031; its renewal was refused on 07/24/2031.
options.outcome: {{DETROIT}} FOOD HYGIENE LICENSE | License expired: 05/20/2031 | Renewal refused: 07/24/2031

options.text: Step up to the serving hatch beside {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps up beside {{Hank}}, who turns to him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANALYZE ENVIRONMENT, first scan (PowerPyx: “When you join Hank, you’ll be prompted twice to use R2 to scan the environment”): the template’s observation group “Scan” with its four clues in the game’s order and text. One scan per visit, each once; the chart node is filled once every item at the truck is scanned (wiki). Scanning {{Pedro}} and {{Gary}} unlocks [COMPANY] (template lock “Scan Pedro and Gary”; PowerPyx says Pedro or the cook, the template wins). The scan includes {{Hank}}’s surname through {{Anderson}}, with a neutral substitute. No stat change.  One repeatable hub; each scan is available once, and joining ends the menu.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} turns on you
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the serving hatch beside {{Hank}}. He turns on you: “What is your problem? Don’t you ever do as you’re told? Look, you don’t have to follow me around like a poodle!”

options.text: APOLOGIZE FOR BEHAVIOR: say you are sorry for how you behaved at the police station.
options.outcome: “I’m sorry for my behavior back at the police station. I didn’t mean to be unpleasant.” {{Hank}}: “Oh, wow… You’ve even got a brown-nosing apology program! Guys at {{CyberLife}} thought of everything, huh?”

options.text: PARTNERS: say that now you are partners, you should get to know each other.
options.outcome: “Now that we’re partners, I thought it would be a good idea to get to know each other better so we can work as a team.” {{Hank}}: “We are not partners. I am a human, you are a machine. So just spare me that ‘buddy-up’ bullshit program, okay?”

options.text: RECONCILE: suggest you forget what happened and start over.
options.outcome: “I think our relationship got off on the wrong foot. We should... forget what happened… and start over. What do you say?” {{Hank}}: “Look, they sent me a piece of plastic for a partner, and I’m dealing with it. But if you think we’re gonna be buddies, you’re as stupid as you look.”

options.text: REVIEW FACTS: suggest reviewing what you know about deviants.
options.outcome: “I thought now might be a good time to review what we know about deviants.” {{Hank}}: “No, now is not a good time to review anything. Now is my lunch break, so just go into standby and cut me some slack, Okay?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO HANK, first menu: the template’s choice group with APOLOGIZE FOR BEHAVIOR, PARTNERS, RECONCILE and REVIEW FACTS in the game’s order. Hank relationship: APOLOGIZE FOR BEHAVIOR small up (+1; template app-relation, wiki “Picking ‘apologize for behavior’… up icon”, PowerPyx “Hank▲”). The other three have no arrow (template; PowerPyx “No Effect”). Options that are buttons in the game show the game’s label first, then a short description; the spoken line is the game’s (the detroitbecometext template resolved against en.json), quoted in the outcome.

nodes.title: {{Hank}}’s lunch
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Gary}} hands {{Hank}} his order: “Here you go.” {{Hank}}: “Ah! Thanks, {{Gary}}. I’m starving…” {{Gary}}, nodding at you: “Don’t leave that thing here!” {{Hank}}: “Huh, not a chance! Follows me everywhere… See…” He carries his burger and an enormous soda to one of the tables nearby. You can scan his meal before you join him.

options.text: Scan {{Hank}}’s drink.
options.fact: {{Hank}}’s drink: an XL soda, 710 kcal, 184 g of sugar, pineapple passion.
options.outcome: XL SODA | 710kCal, Sugar (184g), Carbonated | Pineapple passion

options.text: Scan {{Hank}}’s hamburger.
options.fact: {{Hank}}’s hamburger: 1680 kcal, 36 g of lipids, 53 g of carbohydrates, 2.2 g of salt.
options.outcome: HAMBURGER | 1680kCal, Lipids (36g), Carbohydrates (53g) | Water (53%), Salt (2.2g)

options.text: Join {{Hank}} at his table.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes over and stands at {{Hank}}’s table while he eats.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANALYZE ENVIRONMENT, second scan: the template’s second observation group “Scan” (XL SODA, HAMBURGER, the game’s order and text), then {{Gary}}’s lines and {{Hank}} moving to a table (PowerPyx: “Hank will then take his food to one of the nearby tables. Follow him to continue your talk.”). Scanning the hamburger unlocks [CHOLESTEROL] (template lock “Scan the hamburger”). No stat change.  One repeatable hub; each scan is available once, and joining ends the menu.

nodes.title: At {{Hank}}’s table
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, standing at {{Hank}}’s table while he eats. What do you say?

options.text: [GAMBLING]: ask about the bet {{Pedro}} offered him.
options.outcome: “This {{Pedro}}… He was proposing illegal gambling, am I right?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah.” “And you made a bet?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah.”

options.text: [CHOLESTEROL]: warn him about what is in his meal.
options.outcome: “Your meal contains 1.4 times the recommended daily intake of calories and twice the cholesterol level. You shouldn’t eat that.” {{Hank}}: “Everybody’s gotta die of something...”

options.text: [COMPANY]: warn him that his friends are engaged in illegal activities.
options.outcome: “I don’t want to alarm you, Lieutenant, but I think your friends are engaged in illegal activities...” {{Hank}}: “Well, everybody does what they have to, to get by… As long as they’re not hurting anybody, I don’t bother ’em.”

options.text: HABIT: ask whether he eats here often.
options.outcome: “Do you eat here often?” {{Hank}}: “Most days… {{Gary}} makes the best burger in {{Detroit}}.”

options.text: FREE MEAL: point out that he did not pay for his meal.
options.outcome: “You didn’t pay for your meal…” {{Hank}}: “{{Gary}}’s a friend. I scratch his back, he scratches mine.”

options.text: ENJOY YOUR MEAL: wish him a good meal.
options.outcome: “Enjoy your meal.” {{Hank}}: “Thank you.”

options.text: AREA: remark that he seems to know everyone in the district.
options.outcome: “You seem to know everyone in the district…” {{Hank}}: “{{Detroit}}’s my home. Born and raised. Know most of the guys around here. Went to school with them, or I busted ’em… Sometimes both...”

options.text: Say nothing more and get down to business.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lets the small talk go.

nodes.adaptationNote: The table menu: the template’s second choice group in the game’s order, [GAMBLING], [CHOLESTEROL], [COMPANY], HABIT, FREE MEAL, ENJOY YOUR MEAL, AREA. Bracketed labels are the template’s mark of an unlocked option: [GAMBLING] by watching {{Hank}} with {{Pedro}} (always, on this path), [CHOLESTEROL] by scanning the hamburger, [COMPANY] by scanning {{Pedro}} and {{Gary}}. Hank relationship: [CHOLESTEROL] small up, the chart’s WARN HANK ABOUT CHOLESTEROL; [COMPANY] small up, the chart’s WARN HANK ABOUT HIS FRIENDS (+1 each; template app-relation; wiki “Picking ‘cholesterol’… up icon”, “Picking ‘company’… up icon”; Relationship Stat: “two increases possible”); the rest no arrow (PowerPyx “No Effect”). The game offers several of these lines (PowerPyx: “When small talk is exhausted, Connor will get down to business”); how many is not published, so the benchmark allows up to three, each once, and from the second on {{Connor}} can stop (the benchmark’s stand-in for letting the prompt time out). Options that are buttons in the game show the game’s label first, then a short description; the spoken line is the game’s (the detroitbecometext template resolved against en.json), quoted in the outcome. One repeatable hub, up to three distinct remarks; stopping is available after the first remark. The three-remark cap is an adaptation, not a published number.

nodes.title: Down to business
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Hank}}’s table. The small talk is over; you turn to the case.

options.text: [HIGHWAY]: ask why he did not want you to cross the highway this morning.
options.outcome: “This morning, when we were chasing those deviants… Why didn’t you want me to cross the highway?” {{Hank}}: “’Cause you could’ve been killed… and I don’t like filling out paperwork for damaged equipment.”

options.text: ABOUT {{CONNOR}}: ask whether there is anything he would like to know about you.
options.outcome: “Is there anything you’d like to know about me?” {{Hank}}: “Hell, no… Well, yeah, um... Why did they make you look so goofy and give you that weird voice?” “{{CyberLife}} androids are designed to work harmoniously with humans. Both my appearance and voice were specifically designed to facilitate my integration.” {{Hank}}: “Well, they fucked up.”

options.text: {{HANK}} AND ANDROIDS: ask why he hates androids so much.
options.outcome: “Can I ask you a personal question, Lieutenant? Why do you hate androids so much?” {{Hank}}: “I have my reasons.”

options.text: DEVIANTS: offer to tell him what you know about deviants.
options.outcome: “Maybe I should tell you what we know about deviants?” {{Hank}}: “You read my mind… Proceed.” “We believe that a mutation occurs in the software of some androids, which can lead to them emulating a human emotion.” “In English, please.” “They don’t really feel emotions, they just get overwhelmed by irrational instructions, which can lead to unpredictable behavior.” {{Hank}}: “Emotions always screw everything up… Maybe androids aren’t as different from us as we thought.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s third choice group, [HIGHWAY], ABOUT CONNOR, HANK AND ANDROIDS, DEVIANTS, in the game’s order. nodes.title: In the elevator
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. At the food truck you told {{Hank}}: “I just got a report of a suspected deviant. It’s a few blocks away. We should go have a look. I’ll let you finish your meal. I’ll be in the car, if you need me.” Now you stand in the elevator of a run-down building with your eyes closed. {{Hank}}, from the corridor: “Hey {{Connor}}! You ran outta batteries or what?” You: “I’m sorry, I was making a report to {{CyberLife}}.” {{Hank}}: “Uh... Well, do you plan on staying in the elevator?” “No! I’m coming.” {{Hank}}: “What do we know about this guy?” You: “Not much. Just that a neighbor reported that he heard strange noises coming from this floor. Nobody’s supposed to be living here, but the neighbor said he saw a man hiding a LED under his cap.” {{Hank}}: “Oh Christ, if we have to investigate every time someone hears a strange noise, we’re gonna need more cops. Hey, were you really makin’ a report back there in the elevator? Just by closing your eyes?” “Correct.” “Shit... Wish I could do that…”
facts: A neighbor reported strange noises from a floor of this building where nobody is supposed to live, and a man hiding an LED under his cap.

nodes.title: Into the nest
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the apartment door with {{Hank}}. You knock. No answer. You knock again: “Anybody home? Open up! {{Detroit}} Police!” There is a noise inside. {{Hank}}: “Stay behind me.” “Got it.” He kicks the door in. The apartment is dark, filthy and full of pigeons. {{Hank}}: “What the fuck is this?! Jesus, this place stinks… Uh, looks like we came for nothin’, our man’s gone…”
facts: The apartment the suspect has been living in is full of pigeons. When {{Hank}} kicked the door in, nobody was in sight.

nodes.title: Magazines in the first room
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, just inside the apartment. In the first room to the right of the door, before the room with the birds, two magazines lie on a table. Reading takes time, and {{Hank}} will not wait long.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Red Ice Epidemic
facts: {{Detroit}} Today reports that red ice has become the drug of choice for the city’s growing underclass; analysts suggest it flourishes on the dissatisfaction caused by androids taking human jobs. The main ingredient of android blue blood is among its active agents; the dealers’ motto is “Where the blood is blue, the ice is red... and the money is green”.

media.title: Green Earth: Past the Tipping Point
facts: Green Earth reports that scientists say the planet has officially passed its environmental tipping point: rainforests reduced by 79% since 2000 and coastal corals by 58%, too much carbon in the atmosphere for the environment ever to absorb, and natural resources almost exhausted. “The planet will keep getting hotter now. The only question is, how fast?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s READ “RED ICE EPIDEMIC” and READ “PAST THE TIPPING POINT”, in that order: the two magazines in the first room to the right of the door (PowerPyx), as a media scene: read either, both or neither. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s article pages; interviewees are not named. In the game they can be read at any time during the search; here they come first, and each magazine read counts as one action of the search’s time budget (see C10o1). Neither changes public opinion (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). Replaces the earlier wording, which called the drug’s users unemployed and the room a squat.

nodes.title: Investigate the apartment
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, searching the apartment with {{Hank}}, among the pigeons. In the main room: a poster on the wall, a military jacket, a driver’s license, a bird cage lying on the floor, a chair, a pack of birdseed, a refrigerator and a closet. In the bathroom: the sink, and a wall covered in writing above an overturned stool. Each thing you examine takes time, and {{Hank}} is in no mood to stay. What do you do?

options.text: Examine the urban farm poster on the wall of the main room.
options.fact: URBAN FARM POSTER in the apartment: “Fields in the heart of the city”, 265 Acre Avn. {{Detroit}}. Its corner (POSTER CORNER: 100% recycled paper) was recently moved.
options.outcome: URBAN FARM POSTER | Fields in the heart of the city | 265 Acre Avn. {{Detroit}}. POSTER CORNER | 100% recycled paper | Recently moved. The poster could be pulled off the wall.

options.text: Pull the poster off the wall.
options.fact: Behind the urban farm poster, in a hole in the wall, you found the suspect’s notebook: its writing is indecipherable.
options.outcome: Behind the poster there is a hole in the wall, and in it a notebook. {{Hank}}: “Found something?” You: “I don’t know... It looks like a notebook but it’s... indecipherable.”

options.text: Examine the military jacket.
options.fact: MILITARY JACKET in the apartment: second hand, initials R.T., 90% cotton, 10% synthetic fiber.
options.outcome: MILITARY JACKET | Second hand : Initials R.T. | 90% cotton, 10% synthetic fiber. You: ““R.T.” Probably initials.” {{Hank}}: “He put his initials on his jacket? That’s something your mom does when you’re in first grade…”

options.outcome: BLUE BLOOD | MODEL WB200 #847 004 961 | Reported Missing - 10/11/2036. LED | Biocomponent #9301 | Deactivated: 11/06/2038 - 11:36. You: “Its LED is in the sink.” {{Hank}}: “Not surprised it was an android. No human could live with all these fuckin’ pigeons…” SUSPECT IS A DEVIANT.

options.text: Look at the writing that covers the bathroom wall.
options.fact: The bathroom wall is covered with one sign, {{RA9}}, written 2471 times, among drawings like mazes: obsessive compulsive writing.
options.outcome: OBSESSIVE COMPULSIVE WRITING. {{Hank}}: “Any idea what it means?” You: “{{RA9}}… written 2471 times… Why is it obsessed with this sign?” {{Hank}}: “Looks like mazes or something…”

options.fact: By the bird cage in the main room: SKID MARK - RECENT, trail width 19.6 inches, traces of galvanized steel; FINGER MARKS - RECENT, traces of avian fecal matter, no fingerprints; METAL HOOK, recently broken, 100% stainless steel.
options.outcome: SKID MARK - RECENT | Trail width: 19.6 inches | Traces of galvanized steel. FINGER MARKS - RECENT | Traces of avian fecal matter | No fingerprints. METAL HOOK | Recently broken | 100% stainless steel. The scene could be reconstructed.

You are {{Connor}}, in the apartment. {{Hank}} has had enough: “There’s nothing else to see here… Let’s get out of this shithole before I die of an asthma attack.”

outcomes.hank-jacket: {{Hank}}, at the military jacket: ““R.T.”... He put his initials on his jacket?.. Something your mom does back in first grade…” You: “Deviants have a habit of putting their names on things. It seems important to them.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket [ INVESTIGATE APARTMENT ] as a free search, one action per visit, each once: every clue in the template’s order with the game’s observation text (the poster and its corner, the diary behind it, the jacket, the driver’s license, the sink’s LED and blue blood, the rA9 writing, the stool and its marker pen, the bird cage’s three clues), the two reconstructions PowerPyx describes, the chair (FIND RUPERT), and the wiki’s incidental items (birdseed, the empty refrigerator, the pigeon closet). The HUD conclusions are the game’s THOUGHTS.0501C strings (SUSPECT USED FORGED ID, SUSPECT IS A DEVIANT, OBSESSIVE COMPULSIVE WRITING, SUSPECT HEARD US ENTER, SUSPECT RAN TO THE LIVING ROOM, SUSPECT IS STILL HERE, SUSPECT CARES FOR WILD ANIMALS, SUSPECT DOESN’T EAT; once the sink is examined the game reads DEVIANT for SUSPECT on the forged ID, the birdseed and the refrigerator, and so does the benchmark). Chart nodes: SEE RA9 REFERENCE (the writing), INVESTIGATE STOOL (the stool; the chart hangs it off the writing, so it needs the writing first), INVESTIGATE CAGE, FIND LED (the sink), FIND DIARY (the poster, then pulling it off; cross-chapter), FIND RUPERT (the chair, which needs the cage reconstruction: PowerPyx, “Compete the reconstruction to determine that the android has climbed up into the ceiling”). Whether the stool reconstruction or the LED is also required is not published (research note, open question 1); here only the cage reconstruction is. The reconstructions’ wording is the benchmark’s summary of PowerPyx and the HUD strings. The timer (wiki Connor page: “if he cannot deduce the deviant’s location in time, Hank calls off the search”; PowerPyx: “about five minutes”) is an action budget: eight actions, each magazine read counting as one, before {{Hank}} wants to leave (STAY / LEAVE within C10o1), and three more if {{Connor}} asks for the two minutes. These counts are the benchmark’s, not published. {{Hank}}’s own lines are the template’s and play as time passes: the bookshelf after two actions, the sink prompt after four if {{Connor}} has not looked, the jacket after five if he has not examined it, the window after six. The rA9 line names {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android only if {{Connor}} checked the shower in Partners (string pair SHOWERCLUE / SHOWERCLUENO), read from a chapter 6 flag if one exists, otherwise the second line. No stat change anywhere in the search (template, wiki). One repeatable hub retains its scene ID across all examinations; STAY / LEAVE replaces the examination menu at eight actions in the same hub. The chapter availability hook prepares state-dependent outcomes and sets for the generic clue hub.

Waiting instead of running is the wiki’s first LOSE SIGHT OF RUPERT route (“If Connor waits before opening the door when Rupert runs, Connor will open the door and find that Rupert is gone”), which ends the chapter at RUPERT GOT AWAY with the template’s lose-sight lines (variant “Lose Rupert”, no arrow). It’s alright. Doesn’t matter. We know what it looks like, it won’t get far… Come on, let’s get outta here. Seen enough vegetables for one day…” You: “That shouldn’t have happened. I wasn’t programmed to fail.” {{Hank}}: “Oh well, you fucked up, {{Connor}}. Welcome to the club.”

nodes.adaptationNote: One route fork of CHASE RUPERT. The labels are the game’s route previews, HUD strings THOUGHTS.0501C.CHASEGHOST01 and 02; PowerPyx: “The riskier the route, the closer you’ll get to Rupert, but the more QTEs you’ll have to succeed at (and more opportunities to die)”; a commenter: “you just run towards it”. The wiki: “Choosing the slower or dangerous paths will still lead to Rupert pushing Hank”, so a route’s only consequence is its failure branch: a slow or crowded route can lose the deviant (LOSE SIGHT OF RUPERT, ending RUPERT GOT AWAY, the template’s lose-sight lines, no arrow; the place is one of the wiki’s fourteen), a fast one can kill {{Connor}} (CONNOR DIED, ending CONNOR DIED CHASING RUPERT, software instability small down: the wiki’s “Connor falls to his death”, “Connor gets chopped by a plow”, and “Connor dies by falling off the ladder”, ×2). How the twelve previews group into forks, which fork holds which death, and every probability (8%, 10%, 13%) are the benchmark’s; no source gives them (research note, open question 10). Non-fatal stumbles (the cart, the train tumble, the ladder pull-up) are not modelled. Once {{Connor}} loses the deviant or dies, the remaining forks do not play.

nodes.title: Inside {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: November 6th, 2038, 5:13 pm. You are {{Markus}}. You have found {{Jericho}}: the dark hold of an old ship, where androids who ran from their owners hide. Some huddle by fires; many are damaged. You are wounded in the abdomen and losing blue blood. Three androids stand in front of you, and one of them has just said: “Welcome to {{Jericho}}.” You ask: “Who are you?” “Fugitives… just like you... My name is {{Josh}}.” “I’m {{Simon}}.” A young woman: “{{North}}.”
facts: {{Jericho}} is the hold of an old ship where androids who escaped their owners hide. There you met {{Josh}}, {{Simon}} and {{North}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} looks from one to the other.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint INSIDE JERICHO (no choice), with the template’s opening lines of the section “In Jericho” (date and time NOV 6TH, 2038, PM 05:13; “Who are you?”; the three introductions). The template continues from the previous chapter’s last line, Simon’s “Welcome to Jericho.”, which is quoted here without naming the speaker. The abdominal wound is the one Lucy treats later (the wiki: “Markus’ injury on his abdomen”; PowerPyx: “She will heal Markus’s wounds”); how he got it belongs to the previous chapter and is not narrated. The two prompts that follow use the game’s Jericho script prefix (X0503M) but the template places them here, at the start of this chapter. No stat change.

nodes.title: Who they are
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the hold of {{Jericho}} with {{Josh}}, {{Simon}} and {{North}}, who have just told you their names. What do you say to them?

options.text: TRAIL: say that they knew only an android could follow the trail.
options.outcome: “And you knew that only an android could follow the trail, didn’t you?” {{Josh}}: “Only those who are like us can find {{Jericho}}…” {{Simon}}: “If you could decipher the signs, it’s because one of us trusted you enough to give you the key.”

options.text: ANDROID: ask how many of them there are.
options.fact: {{North}} told you there are nineteen androids in {{Jericho}} still in working order; the rest were damaged escaping their masters.
options.outcome: “How many are you?” {{North}}: “There are nineteen of us still in working order... The rest were damaged escaping their masters...” {{Josh}}: “Many tried to reach {{Jericho}}... Few succeed... Humans have little pity for our kind…”

options.text: {{JERICHO}}: ask whether this is {{Jericho}}.
options.outcome: “This is {{Jericho}}?” {{Josh}}: “It’s a refuge for those who don’t want to be slaves anymore...”

options.text: REFUGE: say you thought {{Jericho}} was a place where androids lived in freedom.
options.outcome: “I don’t understand… I thought {{Jericho}} was a place where androids lived in freedom...” {{Josh}}: “We do live in freedom… It may not be what you hoped for, but here we have no master. We don’t belong to anybody.”

options.text: FREE?: ask whether hiding just to stay alive is their idea of freedom.
options.outcome: “And hiding just to stay alive… That’s freedom to you?” {{Josh}}: “Humans hate us. Hiding is the only way we can survive.” {{North}}: “There is no safe place for those like us. If humans knew we’re here, they’d kill us.”
